title: Golf Course Superintendent
description:
Salary Range: $105,000.00 - $115,000.00
About Sensei

Founded by Dr. David Agus and Larry Ellison, our ecosystem of products and experiences is designed with one intention: to empower you to grow well and lead the world toward greater wellbeing.

Based on Dr. Agus’ philosophy, Sensei believes we can guide our guests to greater wellbeing by offering experiential movement, rest and nourishment classes and programs. The launch of the Retreats wellness brand took place on Lana’i, Hawaii in partnership with Four Season’s lodging and food offerings by Nobu. In this location, Sensei Porcupine Creek, Sensei is operating the lodging operation, as well as world-class golf, tennis, spa, fitness, movement, nutrition, meditative, enrichment and body assessment facilities. In addition, Sensei will run the F&B operation, as part of a licensing agreement with Nobu. Sensei programs and continuing learning sessions are high-touch, evidence-led and supported by the latest technology. You can learn more about our Lana'i golf experience and read our story.

Position Description:

The primary role of the Superintendent is the oversight of the golf course maintenance and related facilities at Sensei Porcupine Creek. This position manages golf course maintenance staff and is responsible for interviewing, hiring, training, leading the team, and performance management. The Superintendent oversees the golf course maintenance, making necessary recommendations and decisions to make to ensure optimal course conditions prevail year-round.

Responsibilities:

  • Schedule and plan irrigation systems, pesticide applications, related recordings, and compliance with regulatory issues.
  • Work closely with, advise, and coordinate with the Director of Agronomy & Landscape on any issues related to golf course maintenance and landscape operations
  • Provide technical, operational and safety training for employees to ensure that staff is working within OSHA, safety, state and federal guidelines for safe working conditions
  • Train and oversee staff in proper and safe operation and maintenance of mechanical and power equipment
  • Hire, train, supervise and motivate staff
  • Schedule, and monitor daily operations, including work assignments and oversight of project completion
  • Make recommendations regarding agronomic planning
  • Oversee employee relations within the department including performance reviews and corrective actions
  • Maintain purchase order system and efficient invoice processes
  • Accountable for the departmental operating budget, monitor, and control departmental operating budget
  • Maintain daily logs & reports to track agronomic systems data, climate predictions, and chemical and pesticide application
  • Maintain knowledge of all technology platforms and applications required for proper maintenance of facilities and grounds
  • Maintain and monitor execution and follow-through of agreed upon daily, weekly, monthly and quarterly communication meetings and resulting actions items and initiatives
  • Maintain a strong unwavering commitment to ensure employees are well cared for in their daily work and that wellbeing activities and opportunities for growth are provided
  • Any and all related duties as assigned by the Director of Agronomy & Landscape
  • Understand the Sensei mission, philosophy and brand standards and develop a team culture around the core company mission
  • Ensure standard operating practices (SOPs) are in place and regularly updated
  • Lead by example with the ability to mentor, inspire, empathize and establish and communicate clear expectations aligned with the Sensei Culture, brand standards of guest experience and service guidelines
  • Be familiar with the existing and emerging health and safety protocols associated with COVID-19 and how such events have impacted our business, guests, and employees
  • Special projects or other duties as assigned
  • Leadership – Maintain a positive, upbeat role, promote, and exemplify Company values and represents departmental objectives and interests to internal and external customers
  • Customer Service – Follow up on complaints, questions, and concerns; respond to internal/external customer needs in a friendly, timely and efficient manner
  • Teamwork - Develop and promote teamwork and cooperation among co-workers
  • Safety – Comply with established safe work practices and attend to all safety-related training provided or made available by the Company
  • Due to the intimate nature of the resort with limited number of guests on property, must assist teams laterally across all departments to lead a seamless guest flow throughout the different resort spaces
  • Other duties as assigned

Requirements:

  • Experience as a Superintendent or Assistant Superintendent
  • Working knowledge of golf course operations, turf management, fertilizer and chemical application, water management, golf course renovation, irrigation, and drainage
  • Experience In employee management
  • Ability to communicate effectively, lead and motivate a team
  • Extensive knowledge of use and operation of all equipment and tools used in golf course and landscaping construction and maintenance
  • Knowledge and understanding of the game of golf, golf rules and methods of play
  • Strong organizational, computer and leadership skills
  • Excellent communication and interpersonal skills
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills

Qualifications:

  • Degree in Agronomics, Turf Management or related field, or equivalent
  • Must possess a valid California driver’s license and maintain a clean DMV record
  • California Department of Pesticide Regulation QAC or QAL or ability to obtain within 6 months of hire

Traits We Value

  • Commitment to a healthier living environment and embracing the Sensei Way and philosophy espoused and science identified in Dr. Agus’ teachings and writings
  • Collaborative mentality and the ability to recognize how to get things done as a team
  • Self-confidence and composure to accept critique, process it, and apply the learnings to improve
  • Resourceful and adaptable, understanding that a big idea can come from anywhere
  • Open to learning, developing new skills and professional experiences
  • Loves a good challenge
  • Resourceful and adaptable
  • A strong sense of curiosity
  • Embraces feedback and constantly seeks to improve
  • Collaborative and knows how to get things done as part of a team

Compensation & Benefits

  • Competitive Salary
  • Robust and comprehensive Health Insurance
    • Medical (100% paid HMO), Dental, Vision, Life, Disability insurance and Voluntary Insurance Plans
  • Employee Assistance Program
  • 401k Plan Matching
  • Tax Savings Benefits Plans
    • Pre-tax 401l Matching Plan
    • Healthcare Flexible Spending Account (FSA) Saving Plan
  • Wellbeing Benefit - Monthly allowance for wellness/wellbeing related expenses
  • Employee Discount Program

We are an equal opportunity employer and value diversity at our company. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, sex (including gender identity or expression; pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), sexual orientation, age, religion, color, ancestry, disability (including association or relationship with an individual with a disability), marital status, National Guard obligation, genetic test results, arrest and court records, reproductive health decision, domestic or sexual violence victim status, breastfeeding requirements, assignment of income for child support obligations, or credit history or report.

title: Optical Components Engineer
description:
About the role

  • Lyte is scaling 4D FMCW lidar into volume production. This role owns the precision optical components that go into our sensors - lenses, prisms, and other optic elements - from first specification through vendor qualification to steady, on-time volume supply. You will be the single technical owner for each component and its vendors. You will drive component specifications to convergence across optical design, systems, mechanical, and the vendor; tie every component tolerance back to system-level lidar performance; hold vendors accountable for delivery; define how parts are tested both at the vendor and in house; and own component reliability through qualification and ongoing monitoring. Underpinning all of it is optical simulation: you will build the modeling capability that predicts how component variation shows up at the system level, and use it to set specs that are both sufficient and manufacturable.

What you'll do

  • Own the optical component supply base - Identify, assess, qualify, and manage vendors for lenses, prisms, windows, waveplates, and coatings. Run technical reviews and capability assessments, and lead second-source qualification in partnership with procurement and quality.
  • Drive component spec convergence - Take each component from first draft to signed-off drawing — surface form and irregularity, transmitted wavefront error, centration and wedge, dimensional and angular tolerances, coating reflectance and transmittance, laser damage threshold, scratch-dig, and environmental requirements. Align optical design, mechanical, systems, and vendor manufacturability, close open items, and freeze specs on schedule.
  • Correlate component specs to system specs - Build and maintain the flow-down from system-level 4D FMCW lidar performance - range accuracy and precision, SNR, signal intensity, and point-cloud quality — to component tolerances. Use sensitivity and tolerance analysis to show which parameters truly matter and where margin can be released to improve cost and yield.
  • Drive vendor delivery - Own component build plans and delivery commitments across prototype, EVT/DVT/PVT, and volume ramp. Track WIP, yield, and capacity at each vendor, flag risks early, and drive recovery plans with procurement and NPI program management.
  • Test at the vendor - Define vendor outgoing inspection and test plans — measurement methods, sampling, and data reporting formats. Audit vendor metrology and ensure vendor data is Cp/Cpk-capable and delivered with every shipment.
  • Test in house - Define incoming inspection and engineering characterization at Lyte — interferometry, MTF, spectral transmittance and reflectance, polarization, and dimensional metrology. Partner with test engineering on IQC stations, maintain golden samples, and prove vendor-to-Lyte measurement correlation.
  • Own component reliability - Define and own reliability qualification for every optical component — environmental and lifetime test plans covering thermal cycling and shock, damp heat and humidity, vibration and mechanical shock, coating adhesion and durability, laser damage, and UV and solar exposure, aligned to automotive and lidar product requirements. Execute tests at supplier sites, in Lyte's internal labs, or at external test labs as best fits each test, and own the results end to end: pass/fail disposition, failure analysis, corrective action with vendors, and ongoing reliability monitoring through production.
  • Build optical simulation capability - Model components and sub-assemblies in Zemax OpticStudio or Code V - tolerancing, Monte Carlo, polarization, and stray light and ghost analysis. Compare measured against simulated performance to root-cause shortfalls, and build reusable models and methods the wider team can rely on.
  • Lead failure analysis on component non-conformances, drive corrective action with vendors , and support MRB and deviation decisions with data.
  • Own component documentation — drawings, specifications, test methods, the approved vendor list, and change control (ECO/PCN).
  • Collaborate across optical design, systems, mechanical, NPI, quality, and procurement, and travel to vendor sites in Asia to support qualification, issue resolution, and ramp.

Required Qualifications

  • M.S., or Ph.D. in Optical Engineering, Photonics, Physics, or a related field — or equivalent practical experience.
  • 5+ years in optical component engineering, supplier engineering, or optical design for production, working with precision optics such as lenses, prisms, windows, waveplates, or coated optics (e.g., in lidar, camera, AR/VR, telecom, or semiconductor optics).
  • Proven track record managing optical vendors from RFQ through qualification and volume delivery, including driving schedule recovery when delivery slips.
  • Deep working knowledge of optical component specifications and fabrication - drawings, surface form, wavefront, centration, wedge, scratch-dig, thin-film coatings, and optical glass and crystal materials — and of the tolerance capability of grinding, polishing, molding, and coating processes.
  • Hands-on optical simulation in Zemax OpticStudio or Code V, including tolerancing, sensitivity, and Monte Carlo analysis, and the ability to turn results into clear component specifications.
  • Hands-on optical metrology — Fizeau interferometers, MTF benches, spectrophotometers, autocollimators, and profilometers — including gauge R&R and cross-site measurement correlation.
  • Experience planning and running reliability qualification for optical components — environmental stress and lifetime testing, coating, and analysis of post-test optical and cosmetic degradation.
  • Data analysis skills (Python, MATLAB, or JMP) to work with vendor and in-house test data at volume.
  • Willingness and ability to travel between the US and vendor sites in Taiwan and across Asia (up to ~25%).

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with lidar, FMCW, or coherent detection systems, and with near-infrared optics.
  • Polarization optics — waveplates, polarizing beam splitters, and prism assemblies — and optical bonding processes.
  • Stray light analysis with FRED, LightTools, or ASAP.
  • Supplier quality practices; automotive supply chain experience a strong plus.
  • Automotive reliability standards, reliability statistics (Weibull, acceleration models), and managing external test labs.
  • Track record of second-sourcing and cost reduction through spec optimization.
  • Prior working relationships with optics vendors in Asia.

Benefits (subject to location and local regulations)

  • Competitive salary and equity
  • Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • 401(k) retirement plan
  • Flexible vacation and time-off policy
  • Collaborative, fast-paced, and inclusive work environment
  • Opportunity to work on cutting-edge technologies with a highly cross-functional team

title: Assembly & Test Tech - Level 3
description:
As an Assembly & Test Tech - Level 3 here at Honeywell, you will play a critical role in assembling and testing complex electronic and mechanical components to ensure product quality and reliability. Your expertise will contribute directly to manufacturing excellence and customer satisfaction.

You will report directly to our Production Supervisor and you’ll work out of our Muncie, IN location on an On-site work schedule.

In this role, you will impact the efficiency and quality of our manufacturing processes by performing precise assembly, conducting thorough testing, and ensuring compliance with safety and quality standards.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Perform complex assembly of electronic and mechanical components following detailed technical specifications and blueprints.
  • Conduct functional and quality tests on assembled products to verify performance and compliance with standards.
  • Calibrate and maintain testing and assembly equipment to ensure accuracy and reliability.
  • Identify and troubleshoot assembly or testing issues, implementing corrective actions as needed.
  • Document assembly processes, test results, and any deviations accurately and timely.
  • Adhere strictly to workplace safety guidelines and quality assurance protocols.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • 1+ years’ experience in assembly and testing of electronic or mechanical components within a manufacturing environment.
  • Strong knowledge of manufacturing processes, quality assurance standards, and safety compliance.
  • Expertise in reading and interpreting technical blueprints and schematics to ensure correct assembly.
  • Proficiency in using hand tools, test instruments, and equipment calibration techniques to maintain product integrity.
  • Ability to troubleshoot technical issues during assembly and testing phases effectively.

WE VALUE

  • Associate's degree or equivalent technical certification in a related field is preferred.
  • 2+ years' experience working in in assembly and testing of electronic or mechanical components within a manufacturing environment.
  • Familiarity with lean manufacturing principles and continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Ability to work collaboratively within a team and meet tight production deadlines.
  • Strong attention to detail and commitment to maintaining high-quality standards.

title: Power Markets Analyst (f/m/d)
description:
About Nexun

Backed by Marguerite, a leading pan-European infrastructure fund, Nexun is a fast-growing renewable project development platform active in Spain, France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and Austria. At Nexun, we are passionate advocates for renewable energy as well as grid infrastructure and are committed to accelerating the transition to a low-carbon economy. Join our diverse team to contribute to projects that positively impact communities across Europe.

The Power/Flexibility Markets Analyst leads the commercial development, negotiation, and optimization of Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) projects, including both standalone storage assets and co-located solar-plus-storage projects. The role focuses on identifying best value and route-to-market for our projects, forecasting revenue schemes and offtake contracts possibilities (Tolling Agreements, PPAs), optimizing the commercial design of our plants to derisk projects and maximize their value at the point of sale (RTB) based on a solid market and technical understanding of electricity markets and asset configurations, negotiating PPAs and Tolling agreements.

Target countries: Italy, Poland, France as priority and Spain, Austria and Germany as secondary markets

Tasks

  • Develop and maintain in-depth knowledge of the electricity markets in at least one of the target countries, including Day-Ahead, Intraday, Ancillary Services, Balancing Markets, Capacity Markets.
  • Monitor regulatory and market developments and evaluate their impact on the revenues and commercial viability of BESS and solar projects.
  • Collect, analyze, and develop electricity price forecasts and revenue projections for standalone BESS and hybrid solar-plus-storage projects.
  • Analyze and compare current route-to-market and optimization models and select and negotiate the optimal role (merchant, tolling, PPA, floor/hybrid structures) for standalone BESS, co-located BESS with photovoltaic (PV) plants, and hybrid renewable energy projects to maximize the RTB value and derisk the projects.
  • Originate, negotiate, and close Tolling Agreements and Power Purchase Agreements (PPAs) with offtakers, utilities, traders, on all type of assets (BESS; collocated etc.)
  • Support the preparation of business cases, investment decisions, financial models, and technical/commercial due diligence processes.
  • Build and maintain relationships with key stakeholders across the BESS ecosystem and the different target countries, including utilities, energy traders, optimizers, aggregators, transmission and distribution system operators, regulatory authorities, investors, and asset operators.
  • Evaluate and optimize different technical system configurations from both a commercial and market perspective to maximize the RTB value (duration, sizing, PV/BESS ratio etc.)
  • Collaborate closely with Development, Engineering, Finance, and external partners throughout the project lifecycle.

Requirements

Technical Qualifications

  • Good understanding of electricity markets in at least one European target market.
  • Familiarity with Day-Ahead, Intraday, Balancing, Ancillary Services, Capacity Markets, and other flexibility markets.
  • Understanding of current revenue optimization and commercialization models for standalone BESS and co-located renewable energy projects.
  • Ability to interpret and use market models, revenue forecasts, and financial models.
  • Strong Excel skills and financial modeling capabilities
  • Familiarity with Python, Power BI, or similar tools is a plus.
  • Exposure to commercial negotiations, tolling agreements, PPAs, or energy trading is beneficial but not mandatory.

Analytical Capabilities

The successful candidate should be able to quantitatively assess how different technical configurations impact project economics. Typical analyses include:

  • Comparing 2-hour and 4-hour battery storage systems with respect to CAPEX, OPEX, revenue potential, and Internal Rate of Return (IRR).
  • Determining the optimal battery size for co-located solar PV projects.
  • Evaluating revenue allocation across energy arbitrage, balancing services, ancillary services, and other flexibility products.
  • Performing scenario and sensitivity analyses covering electricity price forecasts, technology cost reductions, grid connection costs, financing assumptions, and regulatory changes.

Personal Competencies

  • Strong commercial and negotiation skills; proven ability to lead and close deals
  • Strong analytical and structured problem-solving skills.
  • Self-driven, proactive, and entrepreneurial mindset.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills.
  • Fluent English (written and spoken); additional European languages are considered an advantage.

Education & Experience

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Energy Economics, Economics, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, Finance, or related discipline.

5-8 years of experience in commercial or offtake origination, PPA/tolling negotiation, route-to-market, or energy trading, combined with a solid understanding of electricity markets and BESS & all renewable assets. A demonstrable deal track record is highly desirable

Benefits

At Nexun, you’ll be part of a mission-driven, international organization shaping the future of renewable energy across Europe. Depending on the country you work in, you benefit from market-leading compensation and locally relevant benefits. We provide:

  • Flexible working arrangements and a strong work–life balance
  • Market-leading compensation and benefits tailored to the local market and your experience
  • A diverse and international team in a collaborative, inclusive culture
  • Modern equipment, including laptop and mobile phone
  • A vibrant co-working office in a central location
  • The opportunity to contribute to high-impact renewable energy projects across six countries
  • A dynamic, innovative environment that supports learning, growth, and career development

At Nexun, your work matters-here, you’ll be part of shaping the future of renewable energy while thriving in a flexible, modern, and inspiring workplace.

title: BIM Coordinator Infrastructure & Data Engineer
description:
As a BIM Coordinator Infrastructure & Data Engineer, you play a key role in ensuring the quality, consistency and coordination of BIM models throughout the project lifecycle. You are responsible for setting up and maintaining the modelling environment in line with the project requirements and the BIM strategy defined by the BIM Manager.

You act as the primary point of contact for BIM Leads regarding software-related and technical matters and work closely with engineers and designers to ensure accurate and coordinated modelling of the project. You are also responsible for maintaining clean, structured and efficient BIM models, free from unnecessary views, families and non-essential content.

You deliver high-quality BIM models within the agreed deadlines and according to the project's BIM standards and requirements.

Your responsibilities include:

  • Validating the compliance of BIM models with project BIM standards and requirements.
  • Monitoring and maintaining version control of the different discipline models.
  • Periodically merging and synchronising discipline models into a federated BIM coordination model.
  • Identifying design inconsistencies, clashes and unresolved coordination issues through 3D clash detection and model review sessions.
  • Analysing potential causes of design conflicts and reporting findings to the Design Manager.
  • Planning, organising and chairing BIM coordination meetings.
  • Acting as the key point of contact for Design Leads regarding geometric interfaces and associated control measurements.
  • Supporting BIM Leads and project teams with software-related and technical BIM questions.
  • Ensuring the overall quality, consistency and reliability of BIM models throughout the project.
  • Maintaining a structured modelling environment that facilitates efficient collaboration and information exchange between all stakeholders.

Your profile

  • You hold a Master's degree in Civil Engineering, Construction Engineering or Architecture.
  • You are fluent in Dutch and English; knowledge of French is an asset.
  • You have at least 5 years of experience as a BIM Engineer/BIM Coordinator. Experience working on large-scale infrastructure projects (above €25 million) is considered a strong asset.
  • You are proficient in BIM coordination and model management tools, including Navisworks Manage, Solibri Model Checker, Revisto, GIS.
  • Experience with Power BI, Dynamo and/or Grasshopper.
  • You have a good understanding of BIM standards, workflows and best practices.
  • Experience with 4D and 5D BIM processes, methodologies and associated tools is considered an asset.
  • You are detail-oriented, quality-driven and committed to delivering accurate and coordinated BIM models.
  • You possess strong communication and collaboration skills and enjoy working in multidisciplinary project teams.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager, Amazon Fashion & Fitness (F2) Tech
description:
We are seeking a Senior Technical Program Manager to own engineering excellence across the North American Stores (NAS) organization, the teams behind Amazon's shopping and returns experience. NAS is accountable for a widening set of cross-cutting mandates that central teams set, spanning infrastructure cost, operational resilience, security remediation, how fast and safely we ship, and how we protect customer data. These arrive in-year, on the same teams and the same capacity, and this role is how NAS stays ahead of all of them at once. You will stand up and run a new program that holds the organization to a single high bar across five domains and gives leadership one honest read on the whole surface.

You will operate in an ambiguous, high-visibility space that demands deep technical judgment and the ability to build consensus without direct authority. Working with our most senior engineers, you will set the bar for each domain, decompose a sprawling excellence surface into a small set of measurable goals, and drive teams across every organization in NAS to meet them. You will be NAS's single point of contact to the central organizations that set the work, carrying our position and tradeoffs back to them so we shape the mandates rather than only absorb them, and negotiating scope and timelines when a new goal lands mid-cycle.

This role changes how NAS operates, from reacting to each new mandate cold to running from a standing state of readiness, through a model where every organization has one point of contact, each domain has a technical owner, and an automated scorecard surfaces risk before it becomes a miss. You will invent the mechanisms that make excellence a leadership expectation rather than a reporting tax, and you will own the monthly review where the leaders who run the teams engage directly on tradeoffs and path to green.

Key job responsibilities
Program Strategy and Scorecard Ownership - Define and run the end-to-end engineering excellence program across five domains: infrastructure efficiency, operational excellence, cross-cutting mandates, builder enablement, and privacy. Own a single flagship goal per domain and the one scorecard that reports all five to NAS leadership, so the organization has one honest read on the whole surface rather than five disconnected ones.

Central-Team Liaison and Mandate Negotiation - Be NAS's single point of contact to the central organizations that set the work, including SDO, the S-Team, Infosec, and Amazon Privacy Services. Carry NAS's position and tradeoffs back to them, negotiate scope and timelines when a mandate arrives in-year, and represent NAS in central roadmaps so the organization shapes the requirements rather than only receiving them.

Cross-Organizational Leadership and Influence - Drive the domain goals to closure across every organization in NAS, in teams you do not own and without direct authority. Responsible for leading a team of domain owners who are themselves senior technical program managers and engineers, and hold senior managers and their teams to the bar, running an operating model where each domain has a technical owner and each organization supplies a point of contact so one program covers the full surface.

Mechanism Invention and Simplification - Decompose an ambiguous, sprawling excellence surface into a small set of measurable bars, and invent the mechanisms that move them. Partner with Principal and Senior Principal Engineers to set each bar at the right altitude, and retire the mechanisms that add process without moving the outcome.

Review Cadence and Executive Communication - Own the in-person monthly review that NAS technical leaders are required to attend, where leaders engage directly on at-risk organizations and path to green. Produce the monthly flash to leadership covering status, risks, and decisions across all five domains, translating a wide surface into the few things leaders need to act on.

A day in the life
Your day spans the five domains NAS is measured on and the leaders who own them. You start with the program scorecard, looking for the organizations trending off their bar, then pull the domain owners and each org's point of contact together to work root cause and path to green. You meet with a central program team to negotiate the scope or timeline of a mandate that landed mid-cycle, and you carry that back to NAS leaders so no team absorbs it cold. You partner with Principal and Senior Principal Engineers to set or sharpen a domain bar, and with technical leaders across the organization to sequence the work against their capacity. You close by preparing the monthly flash that gives leadership one honest read across all five domains, and by running the in-person review where the leaders who own the teams engage directly on the tradeoffs and decisions in front of them.

About the team
The Fashion & Fitness Tech organization is on a mission to make Amazon the most-loved fashion destination globally through technology. Our team enhances customer satisfaction and operational excellence across the e-commerce platform. We analyze the shopping experience to help customers find the right products and make confident purchasing decisions. Through data-driven insights and cross-functional collaboration with product, operations, merchandising, and technology teams, we identify and implement improvements that reduce friction and increase post-purchase satisfaction. Our work impacts millions of customers while contributing to business profitability and sustainable growth.

title: Java Fullstack Engineer
description:
Hungry for a challenge?

That’s good, because at Just Eat Takeaway.com (JET) we believe everything is possible, or, as we say, everything is on the table. We are a leading global online food delivery marketplace. Our tech ecosystem connects millions of active customers with hundreds of thousands of connected partners in countries across the globe.

Our mission? To empower every food moment around the world, whether it’s through customer service, coding, or couriers.

The Opportunity:

We are looking for a proactive software engineer with a strong backend foundation and full-stack capabilities to join our Identity & Access Management (AuthN/AuthZ) team. As a Full-Stack Engineer, you will bring solid experience in security architectures, identity systems, and distributed microservices to the table.

In this role, you will be instrumental in building high-throughput authorization services, extending enterprise authentication workflows, maintaining developer SDKs, and delivering intuitive frontend interfaces for our global ecosystem.

In this role you'll have the responsibility to:

  • - Build & Scale Identity Services: Design, develop, and maintain enterprise Authentication infrastructure built primarily on Java and Keycloak , alongside high-concurrency Authorization microservices in Go and Kotlin .
  • - Deliver End-to-End Features (React): Build clean, secure, and responsive frontend applications and admin dashboards using React to support seamlessly integrated user and partner identity journeys.
  • - Support Polyglot Ecosystems & Tooling: Support client-side .NET SDKs and write Python automation scripts to streamline developer onboarding, authorization checks, and ops automation across JET teams.
  • - Drive Cloud Infrastructure & Reliability: Package, deploy, and scale microservices using Docker , Kubernetes (k8s) , and AWS , ensuring high availability, fault tolerance, and tight security controls.
  • - Elevate Technical Standards: Implement modern security patterns (OAuth2, OIDC, RBAC/ABAC), adhere to observability standards, and actively participate in collaborative architectural reviews and team knowledge sharing.

What Will You Bring to the Table?

  • - Solid Java Backend Experience: Commercial experience in backend engineering, with a strong primary focus on Java , and comfort working in a polyglot environment (Go, Kotlin).
  • - Domain Knowledge in AuthN & AuthZ: Hands-on experience with identity protocols (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect, SAML) and custom/open-source identity providers such as Keycloak .
  • - Frontend Capabilities: Nice to have hands-on proficiency or willing to work with React (JavaScript/TypeScript) to deliver modern, end-to-end full-stack solutions.
  • - Cloud & Container Experience: Experience operating services in production with Kubernetes (k8s) , Docker , and AWS cloud services .
  • - SDK & Scripting Versatility: Familiarity or comfort working with .NET (for internal client SDK maintenance) and Python (for automation and tooling).
  • - AI-Assisted Development & SRE Mindset: Comfortable leveraging AI coding assistants to accelerate development, paired with an operational mindset focused on monitoring and reliability.

At JET, This Is On The Menu

Our teams forge connections internally and work with some of the best-known brands on the planet, giving us truly international impact in a dynamic environment.

Fun, fast-paced and supportive, the JET culture is about movement, growth and about celebrating every aspect of our JETers. Thanks to them we stay one step ahead of the competition.

Inclusion, Diversity & Belonging

No matter who you are, what you look like, who you love, or where you are from, you can find your place at Just Eat Takeaway.com. We’re committed to creating an inclusive culture, encouraging diversity of people and thinking, in which all employees feel they truly belong and can bring their most colourful selves to work every day.

What else are we delivering?

Want to know more about our JETers, culture or company? Have a look at our career site where you can find people's stories, blogs, podcasts and more JET morsels.

title: Senior Flight Software Engineer
description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

The Senior Flight Software Engineer is responsible for determining how our spacecraft behaves and operates in orbit and building reliable software to ensure it happens. The team is responsible for all phases of development, starting from requirements capture through testing and flight operational support.

Responsibilities

  • Develop reliable flight software that determine how the spacecraft, satellite bus, and reentry capsule operate throughout the entire mission.
  • Write quality structured bare metal, RTOS, or Linux based software for embedded processors in C++.
  • Own all aspects of software development, from design, testing, and integration.
  • Scope projects including requirements capture and initial design trades given open-ended problems.
  • Ensure system quality and performance through software test, verification, and validation (V&V) technique.
  • Teamwork, communicate and problem solve in a collaborative environment.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, math, physics, engineering or equivalent technical experience in safety critical software.

  • End-to-end experience building and launching a spacecraft.

title: Construction Training Coordinator
description:
CAREER DETAILS:

CAREER TITLE: Construction Training Coordinator

LOCATION: AYW Operating Site, Lockhart, TX

DIVISION: YouthBuild

DEPARTMENT: Field Operations and Training

POSITION REPORTS TO: Program Director

POSITION SUPPORTS: Program participants and AmeriCorps participants

POSITION SUPERVISES: N/A

CLASSIFICATION: Regular, Full-time, Non-Exempt



POSITION PURPOSE

The Construction Training Coordinator prepares program participants for entry-level and apprentice-level careers in the construction industry through classroom instruction, hands-on training, and experiential learning. The position delivers construction and safety training, supports industry-recognized credentials, and applies learning through residential and other approved construction projects. Working with program and construction staff, the Coordinator monitors participant skill development, reinforces workplace expectations and safe work practices, and supports participants in developing the technical and professional skills needed for continued training, certification, and employment.


ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND BASIC DUTIES

Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions and basic tasks.

Under the direction of the Program Director, the Construction Training Coordinator will perform the following functions:

  1. Construction Training and Participant Instruction
    1. Develop and deliver hands-on instruction in residential construction processes, techniques, materials, tools, and related construction skills.
    2. In coordination with the Risk & Safety Coordinator, teach and reinforce safe work practices, including PPE, tool safety, jobsite safety, and applicable OSHA requirements.
    3. Coordinate vocational training and credential preparation, including NCCER Core Curriculum, OSHA 10, First Aid/CPR, and other assigned construction or workforce credentials.
    4. Lead experiential learning activities and construction projects that reinforce classroom instruction, NCCER competencies, and practical job skills.
    5. Provide instruction in the proper selection, use, care, maintenance, and storage of construction tools, materials, and equipment.
    6. Integrate blueprint reading, construction math, project sequencing, workplace communication, problem-solving, and other job-readiness skills into construction training.
    7. Assess participant skill development and provide individualized instruction, coaching, remediation, or additional practice as needed.
    8. Maintain instructional and training records required to document participant progress and credential attainment.
  2. Construction Project and Jobsite Coordination
    1. Lead assigned construction activities and projects under the direction of program and construction leadership.
    2. Organize daily jobsite activities and participant work assignments consistent with approved project scopes, schedules, safety requirements, and training objectives.
    3. Provide active jobsite instruction and oversight while monitoring work quality, participant performance, and safe work practices.
    4. Coordinate tools, equipment, building materials, and supplies needed for assigned projects.
    5. Purchase approved materials, tools, equipment, or supplies within established purchasing procedures and authorization levels.
    6. Maintain required project, purchasing, and jobsite documentation.
    7. Report safety concerns, equipment issues, project delays, material needs, or other matters requiring leadership attention.
  3. Participant Development and Engagement
    1. Maintain a structured, professional, and safety-focused training environment that supports participant learning and workforce preparation.
    2. Reinforce program and workplace expectations, including attendance, professionalism, teamwork, accountability, and appropriate conduct.
    3. Serve as a professional instructor, coach, and mentor while maintaining appropriate instructional and professional boundaries.
    4. Monitor participant engagement and identify barriers that may affect successful participation, skill development, or completion.
    5. Coordinate with Participant Services, Career Pathways, program leadership, and other appropriate staff when participants require support beyond the instructional role.
    6. Participate in participant planning, support coordination, restorative-practice, transition, and other multidisciplinary meetings as requested.
    7. Support participant re-engagement and additional skill development when needed
  4. Transportation and Administrative Responsibilities
    1. Safely transport participants to approved construction sites, training locations, service projects, and other program activities using authorized AYW vehicles.
    2. Complete required vehicle, mileage, transportation, and trip documentation in accordance with organizational procedures.
    3. Maintain accurate and timely timesheets, expense documentation, purchasing records, participant training records, credential documentation, and other assigned administrative records.
    4. Provide documentation and information needed for grant reporting, performance reporting, monitoring, audits, and internal program review.
  5. Program Collaboration and Community Relations
    1. Collaborate with program leadership, Education and Training, Participant Services, Career Pathways, recruitment and enrollment staff, and other internal teams to support participant engagement, completion, and transition.
    2. Coordinate with community, school, construction, workforce, and project partners to support training and participant opportunities.
    3. Represent American YouthWorks professionally when interacting with project partners, vendors, community members, and other external stakeholders.
    4. Participate in staff meetings, trainings, professional development, National Service Days, participant activities, and other program or organizational events.
    5. Perform other duties as assigned in support of construction training, participant success, program operations, and organizational priorities.


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Required

EDUCATION / CERTIFICATION

  • Associate degree in Construction Management, Building Construction, Carpentry, Skilled Trades, or a related field.
  • OSHA 500 and NCCER Instructor Certification, or ability to obtain required certifications within the first year of employment.

EXPERIENCE

  • Three years of hands-on residential construction, remodeling, or closely related construction experience.
  • Experience teaching, training, coaching, or providing hands-on instruction to youth or young adults, including individuals who may face barriers to education, training, credential attainment, or employment.
  • Experience applying construction safety requirements, maintaining project or training documentation, and working within established program or project procedures.

EQUIVALENT EDUCATION / EXPERIENCE

  • A combination of directly related education, construction training, certifications, and progressively responsible construction experience may be considered in lieu of the formal education requirement.

Preferred

EDUCATION / CERTIFICATION / EXPERIENCE

  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Management, Building Construction, Career and Technical Education, Education, or a related field.
  • Current OSHA 500 and NCCER Instructor Certification.
  • Five years or approximately 10,000 hours of hands-on residential construction experience, including framing and finish carpentry.
  • Experience managing residential construction projects, including general contracting, project coordination, or construction project management.
  • Experience working in YouthBuild, AmeriCorps, workforce development, career and technical education, nonprofit, or other grant-funded programming.


KNOWLEDGE/SKILLS/ABILITIES

KNOWLEDGE

  • Knowledge of residential construction methods, materials, sequencing, tools, equipment, and common building practices.
  • Knowledge of construction and jobsite safety, PPE requirements, OSHA standards, and safe tool and equipment operation.
  • Knowledge of NCCER curriculum, construction training, credential preparation, blueprint reading, construction math, carpentry, framing, and finish work.
  • Understanding of green and sustainable building practices.
  • Knowledge of instructional planning, hands-on training, skill assessment, and participant progress monitoring.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace, Microsoft Office, shared drives, databases, and participant or project-tracking systems.

SKILLS

  • Strong construction, carpentry, tool-use, and hands-on technical skills.
  • Strong instructional, coaching, demonstration, and facilitation skills in classroom and active jobsite environments.
  • Strong jobsite organization, project coordination, problem-solving, and decision-making skills.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to assess participant skill development and adapt instruction to individual learning needs.
  • Strong attention to safety, detail, documentation, and follow-through.
  • Ability to coordinate tools, materials, supplies, participant activities, and project needs efficiently.

ABILITIES

  • Maintain a safe, structured, and productive construction-training environment.
  • Build professional relationships with participants while maintaining appropriate instructional boundaries.
  • Communicate construction directions, technical concepts, and safety expectations clearly.
  • Exercise sound judgment and respond appropriately to changing jobsite conditions and participant needs.
  • Manage multiple instructional, project, safety, participant, and administrative priorities.
  • Work independently and collaboratively while remaining aligned with program requirements and supervisory direction.
  • Remain composed and professional in challenging or high-pressure situations.
  • Maintain accurate records and comply with safety, program, grant, and organizational requirements.


WORKING MODEL AND CONDITIONS

  • ENVIRONMENT: In-person and onsite with regular classroom, active construction-site, participant-facing, and field responsibilities.
  • INDOORS: Work may occur in environmentally controlled classrooms and offices as well as indoor construction and training environments.
  • OUTDOORS: Regular work at active construction and project sites with exposure to heat, cold, rain, noise, dust, uneven surfaces, construction materials, tools, equipment, and other conditions typical of construction environments. Required PPE must be worn as appropriate.
  • ATTENDANCE: Monday through Friday, 40-hour workweek, with a one-hour unpaid meal period. Occasional pre-approved overtime, evening, weekend, or adjusted hours may be required for construction projects, participant activities, National Service Days, deadlines, trainings, or special events.
  • TRAVEL: Regular local and regional travel to construction sites, project locations, training sites, and other program activities, including transportation of participants when assigned. Occasional travel for trainings, workshops, staff retreats, meetings, conferences, or other approved program activities may be required.


BENEFITS

American YouthWorks offers competitive benefits and leave packages including, on an annual basis:

  • 11 personal days;
  • 8 sick days;
  • 19 break days, taken throughout the spring, summer, and winter;
  • 17 holidays, 2 float holidays
  • Employer contributions toward medical and dental plan;
  • Employer-paid Life, AD&D, and Long Term Disability;
  • Pre-tax programs for child and health care;
  • Supplemental income and additional voluntary life options
  • 403(b) retirement with employer contribution;
  • Employment service awards every 5-years;

title: Principal Memory Subsystem Architect
description:
ADVANCE YOUR CAREER. ADVANCE THE WORLD.

At AMD, we believe technology has the power to solve the world’s most important challenges. From advancing healthcare and scientific discovery to powering AI and the technologies people rely on every day, innovation at AMD is shaping the future.

Whether you’re designing next-gen processors, enabling AI breakthroughs, or bringing leading edge products to market, every role at AMD contributes to something bigger — technology that moves the world forward. Join us and, together, we’ll advance your career.




THE ROLE:

The Memory Standards Architecture team seeks an LPDDR and DRAM Buffer Standards Architect to own AMD’s architecture strategy for low-power DRAM and advanced memory-buffer technologies.

This architect will define AMD’s multi-generation LPDDR and DRAM-buffer roadmap; lead technical positions for LPDDR devices, DDR6 registered clock drivers, LPDDR6 in-package buffers, and future buffer architectures; and represent AMD in JEDEC and the broader memory ecosystem.

  • Own AMD’s LPDDR and DRAM-buffer architecture strategy across business units and product generations.
  • Lead AMD technical positions and serve as the company-wide authority for LPDDR devices and advanced DRAM buffers.
  • Advance AMD positions in JEDEC through proposals, ballots, negotiations, partnerships, and consensus building.
  • Align AMD business units, DRAM vendors, buffer suppliers, and the broader memory-component ecosystem.

Serving Client, Server, Embedded, S3, and other adopting businesses, the architect will consolidate product, platform, design, validation, firmware, package, and system needs into unified AMD positions, supplier requirements, implementation specifications, and platform guidance.

THE PERSON:
You are a recognized memory-technology expert who can move effectively between detailed device and interface architecture, system-level tradeoffs, industry standards, and executive decision-making. You bring deep LPDDR and DDR knowledge, sound architectural judgment, and a demonstrated ability to align internal teams and external partners around technically rigorous, implementable positions.
You communicate complex decisions clearly, resolve competing technical priorities, and build consensus while considering performance, power, reliability, cost, interoperability, qualification, and schedule constraints. You are comfortable leading through influence across organizational and company boundaries.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Strategy and roadmap: Define AMD’s multi-generation LPDDR and DRAM-buffer strategy, adoption plans, priorities, ownership, risks, and business-unit decisions across Client, Server, Embedded, S3, and other adopting organizations.
  • Standards leadership: Represent AMD in JEDEC and related forums through technical proposals, ballots, negotiations, partnerships, and consensus building; maintain approved AMD positions and drive closure of standards dependencies.
  • Device and buffer architecture: Define requirements for LPDDR devices, DDR6 registered clock drivers, LPDDR6 in-package buffers, future buffer architectures, and supporting components, including partitioning, topology, interfaces, protocols, clocking, performance, power, training, telemetry, reliability, security, test, error handling, recovery, and interoperability.
  • System integration: Coordinate DRAM and buffer behavior with controller, PHY, SoC, package, module, board, firmware, validation, and platform requirements; guide tradeoffs among discrete, module-level, in-package, die-integrated, DRAM-integrated, and host-side implementations.
  • Implementation specifications: Deliver architecture, SPD, configuration, authentication, attestation, firmware, power, thermal, packaging, platform, compliance, margining, characterization, robustness, and fault-handling requirements and guidance.
  • Ecosystem readiness: Align DRAM vendors and suppliers of buffers, PMICs, regulators, hubs, connectors, and related technologies on roadmaps, qualification plans, interoperability, readiness milestones, and adoption risks.
  • Cross-functional execution: Serve as the company-wide architecture authority, lead internal workgroups, resolve technical tradeoffs, document decisions and ownership, and provide business-unit teams with specifications, reusable solutions, implementation guidance, issue resolution, and launch-readiness support.
KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:
  • Own AMD’s multi-generation LPDDR and DRAM-buffer architecture strategy, including adoption plans, priorities, risks, ownership, and business-unit decisions, and serve as the company-wide technical authority for LPDDR devices, registered clock drivers, and advanced DRAM-buffer technologies.
  • Develop and maintain AMD technical positions for JEDEC and related standards organizations, advancing standards work through proposals, ballots, technical negotiations, objection resolution, partnerships, and consensus building.
  • Define architectural requirements for LPDDR devices, DDR6 registered clock drivers, LPDDR6 in-package buffers, future buffer architectures, and supporting components.
  • Establish requirements covering partitioning, topology, interfaces, protocols, command and data behavior, clocking, training, performance, power, telemetry, reliability, security, test, error handling, recovery, and interoperability.
  • Coordinate DRAM and buffer architectures with controller, PHY, SoC, package, module, board, firmware, validation, and platform requirements, evaluating tradeoffs among discrete, module-level, in-package, die-integrated, DRAM-integrated, and host-side implementations.
  • Deliver implementation requirements and guidance for architecture, SPD, configuration, firmware, authentication, attestation, power, thermal design, packaging, compliance, margining, characterization, robustness, and fault handling.
  • Align DRAM vendors and suppliers of buffers, PMICs, regulators, hubs, connectors, and related technologies on roadmaps, qualification plans, interoperability, readiness milestones, and adoption risks.
  • Lead cross-functional architecture workgroups, document decisions and ownership, resolve technical tradeoffs, drive closure of standards and implementation dependencies, and provide adopting teams with reusable solutions, specifications, implementation guidance, issue resolution, and launch-readiness support.

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Computer Science, or a related technical field required; master’s degree or PhD preferred.

This role is not eligible for visa sponsorship.

title: Claims Specialist
description:
Job Title: Claims Specialist

Department: Claims

Reports To: Claims Manager



Position Summary:

This position provides expert claim handling services in the areas of coverage, compensability, investigation, evaluation, negotiation, litigation management and resolution of serious and complex workers' compensation insurance claims under applicable law, corporate policy and best practice. Quality claim handling expertise, Service Excellence and indemnity and expense management will also be provided by the position. The claims specialist will also be an expert technical resource to other claims professionals, business partners, policyholders and stakeholders.



Essential Functions:

  • Evaluate, analyze and determine compensability, causation, offsets and exposures of serious and complex workers compensation insurance claims in accordance with applicable law, corporate policy, best practice and prescribed authorities
  • Verify claim information including but not limited to: documentation of the claim history; taking recorded statements from workers and witnesses, identify subrogation opportunities, coordination of medical care.
  • Document all activities in the claim management system. Responsible for outside legal counsel assignments, RTW strategies with policyholders, implement medical case management strategies with nurse case managers and all other expert assignments.
  • Upon determination of compensability: Set and monitor reserves according to company policies and the worker’s injury, issue benefit checks in accordance to statutory requirements, and demonstrate proficiency in the application of state statutes, related case law and to interpret and comply with company claims standards, policies and procedures. Must have above-average knowledge, understanding and ability to apply case law to claim handling practices.
  • Ensure the timely and accurate statutory/benefit payments within the established time frames and guidelines.
  • Prepare and participate in mediation conferences and other authorized legal or regulatory proceedings before the regulatory agencies and courts of law.
  • Maintain a diary on all open claims. Document all relevant information to provide a clear history of events and a proper audit trail. Set review dates based on claim complexity or standard review criteria.
  • Assess and report claims litigation for significant financial exposure, case law precedent or reputation risk.
  • Identify and recommend claims with potential for full and final settlement and negotiate and/or coordinate with authorized outside legal counsel in full and final settlements.
  • Analyze assigned claims to identify trends and opportunities for improvement of policies, procedures and controls, and prepare related reports.
  • Mentor junior adjusters and provide support to Claims Managers as directed.
  • Detect and report reasonable suspicions of insurance fraud by claimants, medical or legal providers, policyholders or other individuals related to claims.
  • Maintain claim records in compliance with applicable law, corporate policies and retention schedules.

title: Snow Removal Operator
description:
SUMMARY:

As a Snow Removal Operator, you are responsible for safely, efficiently, and thoroughly performing assigned snow removal operations while maintaining a high standard of care for Company equipment and customer property.

The Snow Removal Operator operates and cares for assigned snow removal equipment, performs snow removal services according to established Company procedures and customer requirements, communicates effectively with the Snow Removal Team Leads and team members, and maintains a strong focus on safety, quality, and attention to detail.

The specific equipment, duties, and level of responsibility assigned to each operator may vary based on training, experience, demonstrated skill, equipment authorization, operational needs, and the requirements of each assignment.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Safely and efficiently operate assigned snow removal equipment in accordance with Company procedures, manufacturer instructions, and applicable safety requirements
  • Perform assigned snow removal operations at residential, commercial, roadway, parking, and other customer locations
  • Clear snow from driveways, roads, parking areas, walkways, and other assigned areas
  • Follow established routes, work assignments, snow placement requirements, and customer-specific instructions
  • Maintain awareness of pedestrians, vehicles, structures, landscaping, gates, curbs, retaining walls, pavement, and other property features
  • Inspect assigned equipment before, during, and after use
  • Report equipment damage, mechanical issues, maintenance needs, or unsafe conditions promptly
  • Follow all Company safety policies, procedures, and training requirements
  • Maintain a positive, professional, and team-oriented attitude
The duties and responsibilities list is not designed to be an exhausted list of what will be assigned to you. Employees may prefer other duties as assigned by the manager.

QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Valid Driver’s License and acceptable driving record
  • Previous experience operating snow removal equipment, heavy equipment, commercial vehicles, or similar equipment is preferred but not required, depending on the position and equipment assigned
  • Ability to safely operate equipment for which the employee has been properly trained and authorized
  • Ability to understand and follow written and verbal instructions
  • Team player who is able to communicate and work well with others
  • Strong attention to detail
  • Ability to work outdoors in winter weather conditions
  • Ability to work safely around moving vehicles, equipment, pedestrians, structures, and other hazards
  • Ability to occasionally work in a high-stress, fast-paced environment
  • Must consider safety, courtesy, and care for customer property high priorities
  • Ability to recognize and communicate unsafe conditions, equipment concerns, property concerns, or other issues to a supervisor
  • Willingness to work as part of a team and assist with related snow removal tasks as needed

Physical Requirements:

  • Sit for extended periods while operating vehicles or equipment
  • Stand and walk while inspecting equipment and performing assigned duties
  • Use hands and arms to operate equipment controls and perform equipment-related tasks
  • Reach, bend, stoop, kneel, crouch, climb, or balance as required to safely perform assigned duties
  • Lift, carry, push, or pull materials, tools, or equipment as required by assigned duties
  • Safely enter and exit vehicles and equipment
  • Work on snow, ice, uneven surfaces, and other winter conditions
  • Maintain sufficient coordination, awareness, and attention to safely operate assigned equipment

WORK ENVIRONMENT:

The majority of work is performed outdoors and may include exposure to:

  • Snow, ice, rain, wind, and other winter weather conditions
  • Cold temperatures
  • Slippery, uneven, or unstable surfaces
  • Moving vehicles and mechanical equipment
  • Engine exhaust, dust, dirt, and airborne particles
  • Loud equipment and machinery
  • Equipment vibration
  • Residential, commercial, roadway, parking, and other customer properties
  • Low-light or nighttime conditions

WORK HOURS

Snow removal operations are dependent upon weather conditions, snowfall, customer needs, and operational requirements.

This position may be scheduled to work early morning, overnight, evening, weekend, or holiday hours when snow removal operations require it.

As a retainer position, the employee may be contacted and scheduled for snow removal work based on operational needs, weather conditions, snowfall, customer requirements, and assigned routes or locations.

COMPENSATION

This is a seasonal retainer position from October 15 through April 30. The seasonal retainer is starting at (depending on experience) $1,178.57 per biweekly pay period during the Snow Removal season, paid according to the Company's regular biweekly payroll schedule and subject to applicable payroll deductions.

title: Clinical Lab Assistant I (OFNHP)
description:
In the heart of The Dalles, Oregon, Adventist Health Columbia Gorge has served the Columbia River Gorge community since 1901. We are comprised of a 49-bed hospital, various medical offices, home health, a birthing center and a vast scope of services located throughout The Dalles and the surrounding areas. The Dalles is known for its picturesque views of the Columbia River, local charm and delicious downtown restaurants and bakeries. There is something for everyone in this scenic community.

Job Summary:

Collects blood specimens, as well as receives, handles and processes specimens for Laboratory testing. Receives, sorts and accessions specimens, assigning to appropriate pre-analytic and analytic workflow. Completes computerized tasks related to patient registration and/or test order entry, specimen collection, receiving and processing. Performs basic post-analytic tasks, including distributing reports, storing and/or retrieving specimens. Completes quality-related tasks such as documentation of work, maintaining a clean, stocked and safe work area, and monitoring pending work, as well as escalating priority work. Operates and/or uses basic pre-analytic lab equipment. Adheres to all local/state/federal regulations, codes, policies and procedures to ensure privacy and safety while delivering optimal patient care. This position is represented by OFNHP.

Job Requirements:

Education and Work Experience:

  • High School Education/GED or equivalent: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI
  • Associate’s/Technical Degree or equivalent combination of education/related experience: Preferred
  • Experience in Phlebotomy in acute care environment: Preferred

Licenses/Certifications:

  • Certified Phlebotomy Technician I (CPTI) license: Required in CA; Preferred in OR and HI

Facility Specific License/Certifications:

  • Basic Life Support (BLS) certification from approved vendor per AH policy: Required

Essential Functions:

  • Collects blood specimens for a variety of Laboratory tests using age-appropriate techniques; handles/transports Lab specimens and provides post-phlebotomy care to patients. Receives specimens for testing; assesses specimens upon receipt according to established criteria to determine acceptability and takes action according to protocol including escalating to licensed or certified personnel for direction. Handles and processes a variety of specimen types to prepare them for analysis; adheres to protocols to maintain specimen integrity at all times.
  • Completes computerized tasks as appropriate for affiliate to ensure complete patient registration and/or test order entry into the lab information system, as well as generation of collection lists and/or labels. Prepares and/or packages specimens for transport to another Adventist Health or outside reference laboratory and may complete computer steps necessary for processing referred specimens.
  • Maintains an adequate inventory of supplies in work area and/or on phlebotomy cart. Maintains required records by completing basic documentation of pre-analytic and post-analytic work, as well as quality-related tasks. Participates in managing the laboratory workflow by performing duties such as monitoring pending work, escalating priority work, locating specimens, and coordinating specimen recollections.
  • Verbally communicates released/reported results. Routes, distributes and retransmits released/reported results. Stores and retrieves specimens.
  • Receives incoming calls for the laboratory and assists the caller as appropriate or transfers these calls to the appropriate laboratory section or person. Communicates with customer to clarify ambiguous, unclear or duplicate test orders.

title: Director, Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity:

Revolution Medicines is seeking a motivated individual with a scientific background to play a critical role as the strategic sourcing and supplier management lead for drug product and finished product within the Pharmaceutical Development and Manufacturing (PDM) function. This position will be responsible for business and technical operations in support of PDM outsourcing activities and leading strategic initiatives to enable planning, sourcing, production, and delivery of Revolution Medicines’ drug supply, with focus on drug product and finished product. This role is an individual contributor with cross-functional team leadership responsibilities, reporting into the Director, Strategic Sourcing and Supplier Management.

Responsibilities:

  • Responsible for ongoing management of RevMed’s global network of Drug Product Manufacturers.

  • Drive implementation of RevMed’s CMO Lifecycle Management Program across our network of Drug Product CMOs. Support identification, selection, on-boarding, start-up and ongoing management of CMO’s.

  • Lead CMO management activities, including business and manufacturing support, issue resolution, and performance management. Lead weekly cross-functional site leadership team meetings with CMO to ensure all start-up and production activities are conducted successfully on-time.

  • Understand CMO partner internal structure and processes and work with team to ensure successful production, issue resolution and communication takes place to meet RevMed’s production requirements.

  • Lead site issue management and resolution during routine production and escalate issues, when appropriate. Drive risk management activities, including the identification of risks and creation of mitigation plans. Support product transfer activities to the CMO.

  • Establish and maintain effective relationships with key CMO stakeholders to ensure successful manufacture and issue resolution across the external manufacturing network. Foster collaborative relationships with internal stakeholders (e.g. Clinical Operations, Development, Regulatory, Quality, Operations, Finance, etc.) to understand organizational needs.

  • Create and manage contracts, requests for pricing, supply agreements, etc. Ensure activities are executed in alignment with established Supply and Quality Agreements. Work with stakeholders and suppliers to help drive business issues to resolution. Understand contractual / financial implications of issues and solutions and ensure appropriate outcomes are implemented. Manage and communicate forecasts to the sites. Support capacity planning activities.

  • Manage CMO Performance. Measure and report on the overall performance of each CMO. Identify and drive performance improvements (COGS, cycle time, quality, etc.) to ensure efficient, reliable supply of all clinical and commercial products.

  • Work collaboratively with Project Management to ensure projects from conception to implementation and close-out, as directed by management.

  • Serve as Revolution Medicines’ primary business operation lead and project management interface between internal PDM functions and CRDMOs for drug product and finished product by providing adequate oversight.

  • Ensure projects/programs meet desired results, compliance, speed, quality, and cost.

  • Support cross-functional CRDMO management activities, covering all aspects such as business needs identification, market screening, contracting, vendor qualification and set-up, compliant delivery of services, and discontinuation.

  • Work with PDM senior management and cross-functional teams to assess and manage supplier performance through use of personal influence, internal business review meetings, and/or joint governance meetings.

  • Identify and deliver on cost savings opportunities.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • B.Sc. or M.Sc. in scientific field with 15+ years of experience in pharmaceutical strategic sourcing and/or supply chain.

  • Experience working with domestic and international CRDMOs.

  • Experience managing both strategic and tactical/operational projects.

  • Working knowledge of and experience in clinical manufacturing, regulatory, QA, and cGMP requirements for small molecules.

  • Working knowledge of small molecule drug development and commercialization, including, but not limited to, oral solid dosage form development and manufacturing, scale-up, and validation.

  • Working knowledge of pharma end-to-end supply chain, with oral solid dosage form related supply a plus.

  • Strong negotiation skills.

  • Solid project management, facilitation, and problem solving skills.

  • Solid organizational and time management skills.

  • Effective, open, and transparent communication skills (verbal and written).

  • Capable of working on multiple projects/tasks and able to meet timelines.

  • Self-starter with a high-level of comfort with ambiguity and complexity and the ability to multi-task while consistently delivering quality results.

  • Team-oriented, progressive thinker who enjoys participating in an innovative and creative work environment.

Preferred Skills:

  • Experience in implementing and/or managing inventory management system.

  • Working knowledge of commercial manufacturing.

  • Experience developing, negotiating, and executing clinical or commercial supply and/or quality agreements.
