title: ATO /Risk Management Framework Lead
description:
The ATO / Risk Management Framework Lead plans and drives the path to an Authorization to Operate (ATO) and then keeps the system authorized. ACF won't let any production system, MIS, dashboard, portal, data repository, or external facing platform that processes Federal information operate until ACF confirms the authorization path, whether a full ATO, a provisional ATO, or a written ACF OCIO determination that no ATO is required. ACF expects the ATO process to take about six months, on a schedule the ACF OCIO approves no later than 30 days after award. The lead builds the authorization package, coordinates assessment and testing, resolves findings, runs continuous monitoring, and owns the privacy and security activities Task 9 requires, including incident reporting and the flow down of requirements to anyone CDIT brings onto the work. The lead works most closely with the Cloud / Solution Architect, who designs the environment the package describes.

Responsibilities

· Within 30 days after award, lead the draft Privacy Threshold Analysis and Privacy Impact Assessment support package and the Data Security Plan for the COR and the ACF OCIO reviewers, describing data flows, system boundaries, user roles, encryption, access controls, audit logging, retention, destruction, incident response, subcontractor access, and privacy protections (RFQ Task 9.4).

· Work with the COR and ACF to determine the type and sensitivity of the CUI involved and whether an ATO is required, and recommend the most efficient authorization path among the ACF Tech ATO types, including inheritance from a FedRAMP authorized environment and the ACF Authority to Use (ACF Tech Appendix D).

· Propose the ATO schedule for ACF OCIO approval no later than 30 days after award and manage the authorization effort to it (RFQ Task 10).

· Categorize the system under FIPS 199 and FIPS 200 and select, tailor, and document the NIST SP 800-53 control baseline for a Moderate system, applying NIST SP 800-18, NIST SP 800-171, DISA STIG hardening guidance, OMB Memorandum M-05-22, and HHS and ACF policy.

· Author and maintain the authorization package deliverables listed below on the schedule ACF Tech approves, including the annual System Security Plan update, the annual assessment, the quarterly POA&M update, and the annual contingency plan test.

· Coordinate the security assessment with the assessor, support testing, track every finding, and drive remediation or risk acceptance to closure.

· Document the Zero Trust implementation approach and expected maturity level and manage the quarterly Zero Trust scorecard submissions for the system (ACF Tech Appendix B and Appendix C).

· Run continuous monitoring under FISMA and NIST SP 800-137: monthly vulnerability scans with an ACF Tech approved tool, patch management, log review, account review, configuration management, and POA&M updates on the schedule ACF OCIO approves. Report critical and high vulnerabilities to the COR and remediate them within ACF approved timeframes (RFQ Task 10).

· Maintain the authorization boundary and all security documentation throughout the period of performance, and submit changes through ACF change control before implementation.

· Own incident reporting: any suspected or confirmed breach, cyber incident, unauthorized disclosure, lost device, or exposure of information that isn't public is reported immediately, within one hour at most, through CDIT and Guidehouse to the Contracting Officer, the COR, and the ACF Incident Response Team, with logs and evidence preserved and full cooperation with ACF and HHS response (RFQ Task 9.5 and Section 4.0).

· Assess whether any data the program collects, stores, transmits, or analyzes is Protected Health Information and whether CDIT or any subcontractor is a HIPAA business associate, and if so support the Business Associate Agreement and the required safeguards (RFQ Task 9.6).

· Support the Data Inventory and Data Minimization Plan before any data is collected, confirming that no Social Security numbers or other high risk identifiers are collected without written COR approval (RFQ Task 6.3).

· Complete the electronic authentication risk assessment with the system owner and ISSO to set the identity, authentication, and federated assurance levels (RFQ Section 4.0).

· Flow the privacy, security, records, incident reporting, and training requirements down to any subcontractor, consultant, or vendor CDIT uses, track the required training certificates, and keep the records that show compliance (RFQ Tasks 9.2 and 9.3).

· Support the Sustainability and Transition strategy with the security documentation, data handling, and media sanitization under NIST SP 800-88 needed for a complete and secure transfer at the end of the contract (RFQ Task 8).

Required qualifications

· Bachelor's degree.

· At least 7 years in federal information security, with hands on Risk Management Framework work under NIST SP 800-37 and NIST SP 800-53.

· Has led at least one federal system through assessment to a signed ATO, including writing the System Security Plan, supporting the assessment, and managing the POA&M.

· FedRAMP knowledge, including control inheritance from an authorized cloud environment and the customer responsibility matrix.

· Continuous monitoring and vulnerability management with enterprise scanning tools, including reading results and driving remediation.

· Working knowledge of FISMA, the Privacy Act, HIPAA security requirements, and federal incident reporting obligations.

· Clear technical writing and the ability to coordinate assessors, developers, and Government reviewers to a schedule.

· Public Trust Tier 2 clearance, held or obtainable.

Desired qualifications (CDIT additions, not conditions of the subcontract)

· CISSP, CGRC (formerly CAP), CISM, or an equivalent security certification.

· Prior ATO work at HHS or an HHS operating division, and familiarity with the HHS and ACF security program and templates.

· Experience with a governance, risk, and compliance tool used for federal authorization packages.

· Experience producing Zero Trust scorecards against the CISA Zero Trust Maturity Model.

· Privacy credential such as CIPP/G, or experience preparing Privacy Threshold Analyses and Privacy Impact Assessments.

We are currently looking for candidates located within 60 miles of any of the listed hubs to foster more in-person connections while maintaining our flexible remote culture.


GOVERNMENT AFFAIRS SOUTH CENTRAL REGULATORY LEAD

About this role

The Government Affairs Regulatory Lead for the South Central region is the regional large load expert within the Government Affairs team and will support our active development within ERCOT, and future development within SPP. This position is responsible for the coordination of the politics of regulatory issues with relevant teams including Development, Engineering, and the Head of Texas Government Affairs. This role will collaborate with these other teams to address regulatory activity affecting the company’s business interests—including engagement with relevant state agencies such as utility commissions, grid operators and other state agencies as needed.

The role includes external representation with trade associations, digital infrastructure organizations, and NGOs. The individual will strategize and lead campaigns to achieve Intersect’s regulatory goals, ensure alignment of company priorities with political and market realities, and support the company’s growing digital infrastructure strategy. The position reports to the Head of State Government Affairs and works closely with regional Development, Engineering, and Community Engagement teams. The role is based in-region (Austin, Texas preferred) with required in-person engagement across assigned states.

Team overview

This team plays a critical role in advancing Intersect’s mission to accelerate the renewable energy transition by shaping policy environments that enable large-scale energy infrastructure development. What you'll bring

  • Working knowledge of environmental resource issues associated with large energy‑intensive facilities (e.g., energy and water usage, emissions, renewable energy procurement) and ability to advocate for practical, data‑driven policy solutions.

  • Excellent problem solving and strategic thinking skills.

  • Highly driven, detail-oriented, and self-motivated.

  • Ability to summarize complex issues and drive them into actionable strategies.

  • Demonstrated success in coalition-building and stakeholder alignment.

  • Strong political judgment and commercial sensibility.

  • Outstanding written and verbal communication skills.

  • Ability to work effectively in a remote-first environment.

title: Materials Management Principal- SME
description:
As a Materials Management Principal SME here at Honeywell, you will serve as a subject matter expert in materials management, driving best practices and strategic initiatives to optimize supply chain and inventory processes. You will leverage your deep expertise to influence decision-making, improve operational efficiency, and support business objectives within the Industrial Automation sector.

You will report directly to our Supply Chain Director and you’ll work out of our Houston, TX location on a Hybrid work schedule.

In this role, you will impact the company by enhancing materials management strategies that reduce costs, improve inventory accuracy, and ensure timely availability of materials critical to manufacturing and operations. Your expertise will help Honeywell maintain competitive advantage and operational excellence in the Industrial Automation market.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Provide strategic leadership and subject matter expertise in materials management, ensuring adherence to best practices, policies, and governance standards.
  • Analyze, optimize, and continuously improve inventory strategies, procurement processes, and supply chain workflows to enhance operational efficiency, service levels, and cost performance.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders, including Procurement, Manufacturing, Engineering, and Logistics, to drive alignment and execute effective materials planning strategies.
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives and implement innovative solutions to address complex materials management challenges and support business objectives.
  • Develop, monitor, and maintain key performance indicators (KPIs) to support annual planning, operational targets, and executive leadership reporting.
  • Govern and maintain master data integrity in accordance with Global Data Management (GDM) standards across all sites while driving enhancements to SIOP (Sales, Inventory, and Operations Planning) processes.
  • Partner with Production, Quality, Logistics, Finance, and Commercial teams to align material strategies with demand driven approach, business priorities, and operational requirements.
  • Lead, mentor, and develop planning teams across multiple sites, fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Drive organizational excellence through effective change management, process standardization, and the deployment of best-in-class planning practices.
  • Perform other duties and assume additional responsibilities as required to support business and operational objectives.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • 5 years of experience in materials management within industrial or manufacturing environments, demonstrating strong expertise in inventory control and supply chain optimization.
  • 5 years in materials planning systems and ERP software to analyze and manage inventory and procurement processes effectively.
  • 5 years of experience using supply chain workflows, procurement strategies, and regulatory compliance related to materials handling.
  • 3 years of leading cross-functional collaboration and drive continuous improvement initiatives in materials management.

WE VALUE

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain management, Business, Engineering, or related field.
  • Proven track record of successful materials management in complex industrial settings.
  • Strong analytical skills and strategic thinking to optimize supply chain and inventory operations.
  • Experience with ERP systems such as SAP or Oracle.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to lead change management initiatives.
  • DDMRP experience and implementation
  • APICS/ASCM (CPIM or CSCP) and/or Six Sigma Green/Black Belt certifications

ABOUT HONEYWELL TECHNOLOGIES

Honeywell Technologies is a global, pure-play automation company with a legacy of innovating to help solve the world’s most mission-critical challenges, enhancing the quality of life for people and communities around the world. We serve the building, industrial, and process sectors with a broad portfolio of services, solutions, and products, underpinned by our Honeywell Technologies Accelerator operating system and Honeywell Technologies Forge intelligence layer. By combining the deep domain expertise of our more than 50,000 employees with decades of data from our global installed base, we are uniquely positioned to lead the industrial sector’s transition from automation to autonomy. Learn more (https://www.honeywell.com/us/en)

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL

In addition to a performance-driven salary, cutting-edge work, and developing solutions side-by-side with dedicated experts in their fields, Honeywell employees are eligible for a comprehensive benefits package. This package includes employer-subsidized Medical, Dental, Vision, and Life Insurance; Short-Term and Long-Term Disability; 401(k) match, Flexible Spending Accounts, Health Savings Accounts, EAP, and Educational Assistance; Parental Leave, Paid Time Off (for vacation, personal business, sick time, and parental leave), and 12 Paid Holidays. For more information:

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status.

The application period for the job is estimated to be 40 days from the job posting date; however, this may be shortened or extended depending on business needs and the availability of qualified candidates. Job Posting Date: October 2, 2026

THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Industrial Automation (IA) delivers advanced automation control, instrumentation, software, and services that improve the safety, reliability, and efficiency of industrial operations worldwide. IA solutions enable customers to optimize their processes and assets, driving operational excellence and sustainable growth across industries such as oil and gas, chemicals, power generation, and manufacturing.

title: DDM, Process Analyst RGM Commercial Applications
description: This role supports the Senior Product Manager – RGM within Commercial Applications. It is a strong entry point for people who want to grow into data, analytics, or digital product roles, while working on real commercial tools used by senior decision-makers. You will work at the intersection of Commercial, Revenue Growth Management (RGM), and Digital. You will help shape how advanced forecasting and scenario-planning tools are designed, supported, and used in practice, starting with our branded ambient seafood portfolio and scaling to co-manufacturing pet food and frozen seafood. You will not analyse the business or make commercial decisions. Commercial and RGM teams remain the power users. Your role is to understand how they work, help translate that into digital solutions, and make sure the tools run smoothly day to day. What You Will Be Responsible For Understanding How RGM Really Works •	Learn how commercial and RGM teams build forecasts, set prices, plan promotions, and manage mix and trade terms •	Capture how users interact with RGM tools, from inputs and assumptions to scenarios and decisions •	Help translate real-world commercial processes into clear, structured digital processes Supporting Advanced Forecasting Scenario Models •	Support senior colleagues working with: •	Volume and revenue forecasting logic •	Price, promotion, and mix elasticities and drivers •	Scenario planning and what-if simulations (e.g. price changes, promo plans, cost pass-through) •	Help turn business questions into clear modelling and data inputs •	Support testing and validation by checking whether outputs make sense from a commercial perspective Product Operations First-Line Support •	Help keep RGM digital tools running smoothly after go-live •	Act as a first point of contact for users with questions or issues •	Log, track, and follow up on incidents, and escalate when needed •	Build hands-on experience in how digital products operate in real business environments Learning, Collaboration Growth •	Work closely with commercial teams, RGM managers, product managers, and digital teams •	Help maintain simple user guides, FAQs, and in-tool guidance •	Help digital products evolve based on user feedback •	Build a strong understanding of how business, data, and technology connect What Success Looks Like •	You become the go-to person for a commercial tool used by real decision-makers •	You see your work influence how forecasting and scenario tools are used across markets and brands •	Issues are solved quickly, and users trust you as their first contact •	You help turn complex commercial problems into clear, usable digital solutions

title: Program Assistant, (SAGE Center)
description:
About the California Academy of Sciences

Founded in 1853, the California Academy of Sciences is a globally renowned, AZA-accredited non-profit scientific and cultural institution located in the heart of San Francisco’s Golden Gate Park. Home to a world-class planetarium, aquarium, rainforest, research institute, and natural history museum—all under one living roof—our mission is to regenerate the natural world through science, learning, and collaboration.

Our living collection reflects Earth’s vast biodiversity, consisting of nearly 60,000 animals representing over 800 species. Our research collections are the largest west of the Mississippi, spanning nearly 46 million plants, animals, fossils, and cultural artifacts from across the globe and throughout history. Our diverse team includes leading biodiversity scientists, educators, storytellers, designers, and communicators who are passionate about advancing knowledge and catalyzing action through science and storytelling.

Whether you're conducting research behind the scenes or engaging the public on the museum floor, your work will help connect people to the natural world and empower them to protect it.

About the Opportunity

The California Academy of Sciences seeks a Program Coordinator to join the SAGE Center for Science, Ancestral knowledge, and Global Ecologies, a three-year pilot program operationalizing a braided science framework to regenerate the natural world. By uniting Indigenous Science (including Traditional Ecological Knowledge, or TEK) with Institutional Science methods, the CBS establishes an innovative research hub for ecocultural restoration and resilience. It centers on equal partnership and Indigenous sovereignty to empower scholars and co-create culturally grounded, adaptive conservation strategies—such as cultural burns and aquaculture—that inform policy and cultivate lasting stewardship. The SAGE Center is housed within the Institute for Biodiversity Science and Sustainability (IBSS). Reporting to Dr. Shannon Tushingham, Associate Curator of Anthropology and Director of CBS, the Coordinator will be a critical member of a team dedicated to this program. The team's work involves integrating Indigenous and Western methods, drawing on diverse data to investigate climate-driven ecological changes and other scientific problems. This includes collaborating with culture-bearers and Indigenous communities to co-develop research objectives and outreach that honor local protocols. We hope you are inspired by what we do and are excited to contribute to the SAGE Center’s aims and values. The Academy values candidates from diverse backgrounds and experiences and encourages applicants to apply even if they do not meet every single qualification listed.

The SAGE Center Coordinator will work closely with the Director and liaise with internal and external partners. This is a full-time, temporary 3-year position, with the possibility of extension, based as a hybrid role (on-site/remote) in San Francisco, California. The Coordinator will be required to be onsite at the Academy in Golden Gate Park at least 2–3 days per week. Candidates must be up-to-date on COVID-19 vaccination, including receiving a booster shot, as a condition of employment (absent qualifying exemptions). The full text of the vaccination policy will be provided upon conditional offer of employment.

Organizational Culture

When you join the California Academy of Sciences, you become part of a mission-driven community that values curiosity, collaboration, and innovation, and celebrates its accomplishments together. Staff share a commitment to executing a new strategic plan that will strengthen the organization's financial foundations, cultivate a vibrant internal culture, and foster smart growth to secure the Academy’s future.

We hope you are inspired by what we do and are motivated to contribute to our mission. The Academy is looking for candidates who do great work, and we know they may come from a number of different backgrounds and experiences. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every qualification for the position.

This position is based in San Francisco, California. The specific onsite/hybrid schedule for this position is listed below.

This position is part of a bargaining unit represented by Cal Academy Workers United, and will be subject to the terms and conditions of that contract.

POSITION SUMMARY:

The Braided Science Coordinator is the key logistical and administrative support person for the SAGE Center. They are responsible for planning, organizing, and managing research and community programs, serving as the central liaison for all program staff and external and internal partners. The SAGE Center advances community science by uniting Indigenous Knowledge and Institutional Science methods to document biodiversity, foster human-nature connections, collect data critical for ecocultural restoration and resilience, and cultivate partnerships for lasting stewardship.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Program Management & Assistance
  • Provide project coordination and work closely with the Director and Braided Science team to keep the program on track, organize events, and coordinate with the Native American Advisory Board, community partners, and external and internal and team members.
  • Support administration of research, collections, and community programs: message organizers and participants, develop resources, organize files and photos, coordinate and provide assistance during meetings.
  • Support program administration by tracking grant milestones, assisting with collaborative initiatives, tracking invoices and payments, and helping with day to day tasks.
  • Support program success by collaborating and coordinating with internal departments and divisions.
  • Support the preparation of technical reports and assist in the dissemination of results through written materials and oral presentations to both scientific and public audiences.
  1. Partnerships and Community Engagement
  • Serve as a key liaison to communicate with Indigenous partners, external and internal collaborators, and the broader community.
  • Liaise and meet with existing partners and help build new partnerships that support Braided Science efforts.
  • Support the establishment and sustainment of ethical, community-centered partnerships with Indigenous communities, including logistical coordination for adherence to ethical research protocols and metadata practices.

III. Events, Outreach, and Communications

  • Help to develop, plan, and execute community science events and programs.
  • Organize, attend, and manage day-of logistics for, travel to, and hold off-site events.
  • Collaborate with staff to ensure cultural and scientific accuracy as well as accessibility in public programming.
  • Develop media and social media outreach for the Braided Science program; assist with the newsletter, public science content development, and dissemination.
  • Keep the program web pages updated and manage the program newsletter.
  1. Administrative and Financial Support
  • Manage financial logistics including helping with budgets, receipt tracking, purchasing, honoraria and stipend payments, and travel arrangements.
  • Assist with the Indigenous Science Internship program.
  • Support fieldwork, community interviews, and program events in diverse environments, adhering strictly to safety regulations, lab protocols, and collection guidelines.
  1. General & Operational Requirements
  • Follow all Academy safety regulations.
  • Work early mornings, evenings, and weekends, as needed.
  • Other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

We welcome all qualified applicants and especially encourage Indigenous community members or people from diverse backgrounds to apply.

Experience and/or Education:

A qualified candidate will possess a combination of the following experience and/or equivalent education:

  • Experience in project planning and program administration
  • Experience working in research and/or formal or informal science education
  • A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant field (social or natural sciences, education) is preferred, but equivalent professional experience in a highly organized administrative and planning role will be considered.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Organizational and Operational Skills: Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail, plus flexibility and creativity. Must be able to work independently and keep track of program timelines, benchmarks, and communications. Willingness to travel for fieldwork and community engagement. Ability to read and interpret documents such as safety rules, operating and maintenance instructions, and procedure manuals.
  • Cultural Competence and Partnership: Demonstrated commitment to community-driven research and experience or willingness to learn how to collaborate with Indigenous communities and underrepresented groups. This includes knowledge of and willingness to learn more about Indigenous communities and human-nature connections, and a strong interest in the human and natural world.
  • Ethical and Equitable Practice: Understanding of and commitment to collaborative research and developing ethical metadata project practices. Committed to working on a team that is striving to be anti-racist in work, interactions, systems, and tools.
  • Communication and Collaboration: Confident and flexible communicator, both written and verbal, to diverse audiences. Works well as part of multi-disciplinary teams, diverse stakeholder groups, and independently, and has the demonstrated ability to successfully collaborate with non-scientists.

Physical Environment:
To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential job duty satisfactorily. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable qualified individuals with disabilities to perform essential job functions. While performing the duties of this job, the employee is frequently required to stand, sit, walk, use a computer, and communicate on the phone, in person, and online meetings/calls. The employee will spend time out-of-doors at events and programs, occasionally in hot or inclement weather. Must be able to transport 30 lbs. Must be able to perform repetitive motions 50% of the time.

Compensation and Benefits:
The salary range for this position is $35.78- $37.23. Actual compensation will be commensurate with the final candidate's qualifications and experience, including skills, knowledge, relevant education, certifications and aligned with the internal peer group. We believe in fair and equitable compensation practices and are committed to providing competitive salaries within the industry and market standards. The Academy offers a total compensation package that emphasizes both base salary and comprehensive benefits based on the hours per week worked. Further details regarding compensation and benefits will be discussed during the interview process.

Schedule: Full-time, temporary, 40 hours per week. Hybrid schedule with three days onsite and two days remote.

How to Apply: Interested candidates should submit a resume and application through our Careers Page portal.

title: Senior Remote Sensing Data Scientist, Cal/Val
description:
About the role

Muon Space is building a family of infrared imaging missions designed for global wildfire detection and monitoring, weather and cloud characterization, and space-based environmental monitoring. Muon's IR Data Products team builds the analytics system that processes the data from our spacecraft's custom multispectral imaging instruments into data products and analytics for diverse end-user stakeholders from these missions. We are seeking a Data Scientist to join the team to build out the on-orbit data calibration system.

In this role, the candidate will join Muon's calibration team to build the production software systems that deliver calibration and image processing of the unique multi-spectral infrared data from several instrument variations in Muon's IR missions. This is a data science role with a strong software engineering focus: the successful candidate will translate calibration algorithms into hardened production pipelines, complete with monitoring and alerting, unit and integration testing, and automated diagnostic visualizations that keep calibration and image quality observable end-to-end. As the FireSat constellation scales, this role will take on an expanded mandate that spans both the FireSat Initial Operating Capability (IOC) commissioning and Muon's Space-Based Environmental Monitoring (SBEM) program. In the near term, the candidate will build out and operate the calibration software stack for the three FireSat satellites of the IOC constellation and stand up the automated testing and monitoring tooling that keeps that stack healthy at constellation scale. In parallel, the candidate will develop the production calibration infrastructure for Muon's SBEM instruments — a next-generation sensor suite featuring additional infrared spectral bands and significantly more stringent radiometric calibration requirements than the FireSat camera. As the SBEM program advances toward its 2027 launch, the candidate will first collaborate with the IR Instrument team on pre-launch calibration software and test harnesses, then lead the deployment and on-orbit operation of the SBEM calibration pipelines.

This position is hybrid and requires working on-site in our Denver, CO office three days per week.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and operate production-grade calibration and image-processing pipelines for the multispectral infrared imagery from Muon's FireSat and SBEM missions.
  • Translate calibration algorithms — such as dark/offset correction, non-uniformity correction (NUC), radiometric gain and linearity, bad-pixel identification and replacement, and band-to-band registration — from research prototypes into hardened, well-tested production code, and own the testing strategy across unit, integration, and regression suites over representative lab and on-orbit datasets.
  • Analyze pre-launch (thermal-vacuum, integrating sphere) and on-orbit calibration data to derive, validate, and trend calibration coefficients, and build monitoring, alerting, and automated diagnostic visualizations that surface calibration accuracy, noise, uniformity, and image-quality metrics as data flows through the pipelines.
  • Contribute to CI/CD, deployment, containerization, and observability tooling that keeps calibration services reliable in production, and partner with calibration scientists and the IR Instrument team to plan and execute pre-launch and on-orbit calibration campaigns for the SBEM instruments and productionize their algorithms.
  • Drive engineering best practices across the calibration codebase — code review, version control, documentation, versioned management of calibration coefficients and lookup tables, and continuous improvement of test coverage and reliability.
  • Work cross-functionally with calibration scientists, IR instrument engineers, and product teams to build and maintain operational calibration services and ensure the scientific quality, quantitative validation, and radiometric integrity of Muon's IR data products — including uncertainty budgets and cross-calibration against on-board calibrators, blackbody references, and vicarious calibration sites
  • Learn new topics as needed (measurement techniques, geospatial data engineering, software engineering, customer domain-specific implications)

Qualifications

  • PhD with 3+ years, MS with 6+ years, or BS with 8+ years of industry experience
  • 4+ years of experience calibrating imaging instruments
  • Hands-on experience with complex data from new imaging instruments
  • Proven track record shipping and operating production data or analytics pipelines for scientific data — including monitoring, logging, alerting, and automated testing — ideally in a remote sensing, calibration, or other measurement-instrument context
  • Demonstrated experience taking scientific or numerical algorithms — for example calibration, image-processing, or signal-processing algorithms — from prototype to hardened, maintainable production code, including designing unit and integration test suites and quantitative validation against reference data
  • Exceptional Python software engineering skills, including modern packaging, testing frameworks (e.g., pytest), version control, code review, and CI/CD workflows
  • Solid grounding in statistics, applied mathematics, and enough instrument physics to reason about calibration algorithms, radiometric error budgets, and their diagnostics — and to design meaningful automated quality visualizations on top of them
  • Ability to work with a distributed, interdisciplinary team (scientists, engineers, data support)
  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced start up environment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with mid-wave infrared instruments and MWIR data processing, and hands-on experience calibrating on-orbit imaging instruments — radiometric, spectral, and geometric

  • Lead, coach, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of technology professionals.

  • Establish clear expectations and provide ongoing performance feedback and development opportunities.

Required Qualifications

  • Strong understanding of application delivery, support, operations, and service level management.

What Success Looks Like

Successful candidates will be able to:

  • Balance competing priorities while maintaining operational excellence.

You'll join a collaborative organization where leadership is measured not only by results, but by the ability to develop talent, strengthen relationships, inspire innovation, and create lasting business value.

As the Director, IT Applications, you'll have the opportunity to influence enterprise technology strategy, lead meaningful transformation initiatives, mentor future leaders, and help advance solutions that support the health and well-being of the communities we serve.

Ready to make a lasting impact? Apply today and help shape the future of technology at Liberty Dental Plan.

title: Workflow Consultant & Trainer
description:
Elation Health is transforming primary care through a cloud-based clinical platform designed to improve both physician and patient quality of life. Our mission is to strengthen the relationship between patients and physicians by creating clinical-first technology that supports value-based care and streamlines clinician workflows.

Serving thousands of independent practices, medical groups, and risk-bearing entities across the country, Elation helps providers deliver exceptional care while meeting the operational and financial demands of modern healthcare.

We are seeking a highly motivated, bilingual Workflow Consultant & Trainer based in Southern California to lead onboarding, training, and workflow optimization efforts within our most strategic enterprise partner networks.

This role is centered on enabling providers and their teams to fully adopt and maximize Elation Health's platform through hands-on training, live and virtual instruction, and ongoing workflow consultation. The ideal candidate brings deep cultural competency and fluency in Korean and English, building lasting trust within the communities we serve.

You'll serve as the primary training and workflow resource embedded within our enterprise partner ecosystem, running structured training sessions, developing practice-specific workflows, and ensuring providers confidently adopt Elation. Expect 100% on-the-ground presence across partner sites, clinics, and community events.

This is a part-time contract role (30 hours/week) with a three-month review.

Responsibilities

Training Delivery — Live & Virtual

  • Design and lead bilingual (Korean and English) onboarding and training sessions for providers, clinical staff, and practice administrators across enterprise partner networks.
  • Deliver both in-person training at practice sites and structured virtual sessions via video conferencing tools.
  • Build and maintain a library of training materials, workflows, quick reference guides, and session recordings in both languages.
  • Run role-specific training tracks for physicians, MAs, front desk, and practice managers, ensuring each stakeholder understands their workflow within Elation.
  • Facilitate group training workshops, one-on-one coaching sessions, and refresher trainings post-go-live.

Workflow Consultation

  • Partner with practices to assess current workflows and map them to Elation's clinical platform, identifying gaps, inefficiencies, and optimization opportunities.
  • Provide tailored workflow recommendations that align with each practice's specialty, care model, and value-based care requirements.
  • Guide providers through best practices for clinical documentation, care gap workflows, quality measure tracking, and EHR utilization.
  • Collaborate with implementation and customer success teams to ensure workflow designs are scalable and sustainable.

Community & Provider Engagement

  • Represent Elation Health at local provider events, workshops, and seminars, educating providers about the platform and building awareness of Elation's capabilities.
  • Engage directly with providers and healthcare communities to build trust and credibility through culturally resonant communication.

title: Registered Vascular Technologist
description:
Metro Vein Centers is a rapidly growing healthcare practice specializing in state-of-the-art vein treatments. Our board-certified physicians and expert staff are on a mission to improve people’s quality of life by relieving the painful, yet highly treatable symptoms of vein disease—such as varicose veins and heavy, aching legs.

With over 70 clinics across 8 states, and still growing, we’re building the future of vein care—delivering compassionate, results-driven care in a modern, patient-first environment.

We proudly maintain a Net Promoter Score (NPS) of 93, the highest patient satisfaction in the industry.

About the Role

Metro Vein Centers is seeking a Vascular Ultrasound Technologist (RVT, RVS, ARRT, or board-eligible graduate) to join our growing clinic.

This is an excellent opportunity for vascular sonographers seeking a consistent Monday-Friday outpatient schedule in a collaborative, patient-focused environment. Our ultrasound technologists play a critical role in diagnosing venous disease and helping patients improve their quality of life.

Whether you are an experienced vascular technologist or a recent graduate eligible to sit for registry certification, we provide structured training, strong physician collaboration, and the opportunity to grow within one of the nation’s fastest-growing vein practices.

At Metro Vein Centers, our RVTs are a critical extension of our physicians—ensuring every ultrasound scan supports accurate diagnoses, procedural success, and exceptional patient care.

What Your Day Looks Like

  • Ability to thrive in a fast-paced outpatient clinical environment

Preferred Experience

This Role Is Great For Candidates With Experience In:

Compensation

Competitive base compensation based on experience

The Metro Vein Centers Difference

Healthy legs. Happier lives.
At Metro Vein Centers, we believe exceptional care begins with an exceptional experience. Our mission is to make vein care approachable, empowering, and connected to overall well-being. From the first conversation to the final follow-up, every patient interaction reflects our commitment to compassion, expertise, and trust.

title: Senior AI/ML & Mobile Application Engineer (iOS/Android) - Remote
description:
This is a remote position.

Job timings: Mon - Fri US EST time zone
Job Location: Pakistan (Remote)
Experience: 5+ years

ROLE OVERVIEW

We are looking for a Senior AI/ML & Mobile Application Engineer (iOS/Android) responsible for designing, training, deploying, and optimizing AI/ML models that power our Voice Agent platform, while also contributing to the development and integration of Android and iOS applications.

This role spans the full AI lifecycle—from research and experimentation to production deployment and monitoring—and requires hands-on mobile application development experience. The ideal candidate will have deep expertise in speech and NLP technologies, strong engineering practices, and experience integrating AI-powered capabilities into mobile applications.
The role requires collaboration across backend, frontend, mobile, and infrastructure teams. Frontend and mobile application development experience are mandatory, as the position includes building prototypes, dashboards, internal demos, and production-ready mobile experiences.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
  • Model Development: Design, train, and fine-tune models and pipelines for STT, NLU, and TTS use cases.
  • MLOps: Build and maintain MLOps pipelines for model deployment, monitoring, and retraining.
  • API Development: Develop APIs and services that expose AI capabilities to backend, frontend, and mobile applications.
  • Performance Optimization: Collaborate with backend engineers to optimize inference performance and end-to-end latency.
  • Mobile Application Development: Develop, enhance, and maintain applications for Android and iOS, including integration of AI/ML and Voice Agent capabilities.
  • Mobile AI Integration: Integrate APIs, speech processing, real-time communication, and AI-powered functionality into mobile applications.
  • Frontend Prototyping: Create frontend prototypes, dashboards, and demonstrations using a modern frontend framework.
  • Research & Experimentation: Conduct research and controlled experiments to improve model accuracy, quality, and performance.
  • Vendor Evaluation: Evaluate external models and providers against product requirements and measurable benchmarks.
  • Documentation: Document model architectures, experiments, evaluation results, mobile integrations, and deployment processes.
  • Code Quality: Participate in code reviews and maintain high engineering and reproducibility standards.

Requirements

  • Experience: 7–9 years of relevant software engineering and AI/ML development experience.
  • Programming: Strong Python expertise with experience in PyTorch, TensorFlow, Hugging Face, or equivalent frameworks.
  • Speech & NLP: Hands-on experience with speech/audio processing and natural language processing techniques.
  • Model Deployment: Hands-on deployment experience using ONNX, TensorRT, Triton, or equivalent tooling.
  • Android Development: Hands-on experience developing Android applications using Kotlin and/or Java.
  • iOS Development: Hands-on experience developing iOS applications using Swift and/or Objective-C.
  • Mobile Integration: Experience integrating REST APIs, SDKs, authentication, real-time communication, and AI-powered services into mobile applications.
  • Frontend (Mandatory): Experience with React, Vue.js, or Angular.
  • Cloud AI Platforms: Experience with AWS SageMaker, GCP Vertex AI, Azure ML, or an equivalent cloud AI platform.
  • Containerization: Knowledge of Docker and Kubernetes.
  • Version Control & CI/CD: Experience with Git and continuous integration and delivery pipelines.
  • Analytical Skills: Strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
PREFERRED SKILLS
  • Experience with real-time streaming using WebSocket or WebRTC.
  • Experience building voice-enabled or AI-powered Android/iOS applications.
  • Experience with mobile audio capture, playback, streaming, and speech processing.
  • Knowledge of model quantization, pruning, and inference optimization.
  • Familiarity with SIP, WebRTC, or PSTN integration.
  • Experience deploying or optimizing AI models for mobile or edge devices.

description:
IT Security Analyst – Entry Level

State of South Carolina

At least 6 months of valid work authorization
(Citizen, GC, EAD, OPT-EAD, H4-EAD)

Tentative Start Date

11/16/2026

Deadline

10/08/2026


Project Overview

The South Carolina Department of Motor Vehicles (SCDMV) is focused on maintaining secure and efficient IT systems that protect sensitive citizen information and ensure the integrity of motor vehicle licensing and titling data. The objective of this engagement is to strengthen the agency’s overall security posture, safeguard critical systems and data, reduce security risks, and support a security-focused IT environment that maintains public trust.


Duties/Responsibilities:

Entry-Level Security Position

  • Support the DMV Security Team in day-to-day cybersecurity activities.
  • Receive training to perform assigned security responsibilities.
  • Apply basic server or network administration skills as a foundation for cybersecurity responsibilities.

Threat Intelligence Research

  • Monitor and analyze threat intelligence feeds to identify emerging threats relevant to the organization.
  • Document new attack methods, vulnerabilities, and other threat findings.
  • Share relevant threat intelligence findings with the security team.
  • Use open-source intelligence (OSINT) tools to gather data on potential risks and adversaries.

Threat Hunting and Detection Rule Creation

  • Conduct proactive searches for suspicious behavior in network and endpoint activity using provided tools and playbooks.
  • Utilize threat feeds to support threat-hunting activities.
  • Investigate suspicious activity across network and endpoint environments.
  • Stay current on emerging cybersecurity threats.
  • Collaborate with senior analysts to refine and test detection rules.
  • Assist with SIEM queries and Microsoft Defender for Endpoint detection rules.
  • Document threat-hunting methodologies and findings to support continuous improvement.

Log Analysis

  • Review and interpret firewall, endpoint, and server logs.
  • Identify indicators of compromise (IOCs).
  • Identify anomalous IP addresses, unauthorized access attempts, and other suspicious activity.
  • Escalate identified security findings to senior analysts.
  • Maintain records of recurring patterns and anomalies for long-term tracking and analysis.

Incident Response

  • Assist with the initial triage of cybersecurity incidents.
  • Follow incident response frameworks such as NIST and MITRE ATT&CK.
  • Identify and escalate potential security threats.
  • Gather relevant evidence during security incidents.
  • Analyze logs and alert data to determine the scope and severity of incidents.
  • Document findings during incident investigations.
  • Contribute to incident containment and remediation efforts.

Documentation, Reporting, and Communication

  • Create clear and detailed incident reports.
  • Prepare after-action reviews following security incidents.
  • Develop and maintain security process documentation.
  • Deliver reports on the organization’s security posture.
  • Propose appropriate security mitigation strategies.
  • Draft training materials and security guides to improve organizational awareness and readiness.
  • Regularly update and organize documentation to maintain accuracy and accessibility for team use.

Vulnerability Management

  • Analyze vulnerability reports.
  • Prioritize patching and remediation activities.
  • Understand and apply NIST best practices related to vulnerability management.
  • Security Awareness Training
  • Develop security awareness training.
  • Deliver security awareness training to employees.
  • Conduct or support security awareness simulations.
  • Assess employee security awareness through simulations.

Security Automation and Scripting

  • Leverage SCCM for patch deployment.
  • Use Group Policy (GPO) to support patch deployment and security administration.
  • Use PowerShell for patch deployment and automation.
  • Automate tasks beyond SCCM, GPO, and PowerShell to increase operational efficiency.

Endpoint and Network Security

  • Configure endpoint security policies.
  • Analyze endpoint security alerts.
  • Manage and support endpoint protection.
  • Apply knowledge of network protocols to security activities.
  • Apply knowledge of firewalls to strengthen network security.
  • Support efforts to improve the organization’s overall security posture.

Digital Forensics and Cloud Security

  • Investigate cybersecurity incidents.
  • Collect evidence related to security incidents for deeper analysis.
  • Support digital forensic investigation activities.
  • Develop knowledge of cloud-specific security solutions.
  • Support security requirements as the organization’s cloud adoption grows.


Requirements

Education and Certifications:

  • High School Diploma is required; minimum GIAC Security Essentials (GSEC)
  • CompTIA Security+
  • CompTIA Network+
  • GIAC Certified Incident Handler (GCIH)


Required Skills:

· Understanding of security concepts and processes.

· Understanding of basic computer and network concepts.


Preferred Skills:

  • 1+ year of experience in an IT security-focused role.
  • Experience with SIEM and endpoint security tools.
  • Experience with PowerShell, Group Policy (GPO), and endpoint management.
  • Knowledge of vulnerability management and cloud security.
  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or a related field.
  • 1+ year of experience in server or network administration.


Additional Skills:

  • Problem-Solving: Ability to analyze data, identify anomalies, and recommend appropriate solutions.
  • Attention to Detail: Ability to perform accurate analysis and configuration to support effective security measures.
  • Team Collaboration & Communication: Ability to communicate clearly and work effectively within a mid-sized team environment.


Benefits

Standard Employee Benefits.
50% Health Insurance Paid by Innosoft, Paid Vacation, 401K Match, STD LTD and AD&D paid by Innosoft.

title: Storeperson
description:

title: Senior Program Manager, Project Logistics – Data Center Supply Chain
location: Redwood City, CA; San Diego, CA; Denver, CO; Phoenix, AZ; Austin, TX
description:
Do you want to work with high-caliber professionals in a dynamic and growing company? Are you entrepreneurial, hard-working, and collegial? Join us at SB Energy, a leading infrastructure company backed by SoftBank Group and Ares Infrastructure, pairing cutting-edge innovation with best-in-class execution. Our mission is to deliver reliable and secure data center and power infrastructure to strengthen America's future.

Founded in 2019, SB Energy is a SoftBank Group company headquartered in Redwood City, California. In 2026, SoftBank Group and OpenAI announced a $1 billion investment to support SB Energy as their leading development and execution partner for data center campuses, while Ares Infrastructure continues its long-standing support of the company's growth. SB Energy develops, builds, owns, and operates some of the largest and most technically advanced energy and data center infrastructure projects in the United States. Since its founding, the company has rapidly grown into a top-tier integrated platform with more than 3 gigawatts (GW) in operation and a multi-GW pipeline of energy and data center infrastructure nationwide.

SB Energy also leverages a strong culture of innovation to identify and integrate new technologies into its projects, including its AI-based digital platform, delivering energy infrastructure that is local, reliable, and matched to load. We are building the energy and infrastructure future—today.

Come join us in accelerating the energy and infrastructure transition!

Basic Function

As a member of the Data Center Supply Chain team, the Senior Program Manager, Project Logistics will lead domestic movement of high-value, long-lead owner-furnished, contractor-installed (OFCI) equipment from the agreed OEM handoff through delivery to the defined receiving point. The role directs qualified primary transport providers for project cargo, oversized/overweight moves, heavy haul, specialized final mile and recovery. The role protects schedule, equipment condition and cost while coordinating readiness and receiving requirements with the Control Tower and Storage/Site lead.

SB Energy is building a procurement team under a common role profile, bringing together complementary electrical, mechanical, commercial, and logistics strengths. Within this team, this role focuses on transportation and project logistics, including transportation planning, project cargo, and site delivery. The manager may lead transportation and logistics activities for an individual project, manage equipment movements across multiple projects, or lead a shared transportation or logistics planning assignment.

Assignments may evolve as projects advance, workloads shift, and business priorities change. The manager is expected to contribute beyond their primary area, including broader procurement, sourcing, supplier development, or planning assignments, based on relevant experience, equipment knowledge, readiness, workload, and appropriate specialist support. Each manager maintains clear ownership of assigned responsibilities, cross-trains colleagues, and provides structured handoffs and backup coverage.

Candidates must demonstrate depth in transportation and project logistics, together with the flexibility and willingness to build capability across the broader function. Candidates are not expected to be specialists in every electrical, mechanical, commercial, or logistics discipline.

Responsibilities

  • Transportation Planning: Build domestic movement plans linked to equipment and PO records, the agreed OEM handoff, approved Required on Site Dates, Control Tower supplier readiness, storage capacity and construction sequence. Select qualified road, rail or other domestic modes for the actual route and equipment.
  • Project Cargo and Delivery: Direct qualified providers to complete route surveys, permits, escorts, load plans, transport engineering, and handling methods. Obtain designated Engineering and site approvals; coordinate access, unloading and rigging interfaces, receiving windows, and backup capacity.
  • Shipment Release: Authorize domestic dispatch within delegated authority after applicable OEM handoff, supplier readiness, transport, storage and receiving-site gates clear. Confirm packaging, dimensions, weight, insurance, authorized service scope and evidence. Record holds and resume only after designated clearance.
  • Execution and Recovery: Direct provider execution and resolve milestone delays, capacity gaps, port disruption, failed deliveries, and time-critical recovery. Keep planned, forecast, and actual dates distinct. Escalate decisions beyond delegated authority with options, cost and schedule exposure, and a decision deadline.
  • Provider and Commercial Management: Manage forwarders, carriers, lead logistics providers, and project-cargo specialists under approved agreements, rates, allocation rules, and service levels. Define transport requirements for service schedules and statements of work with Procurement, Legal, Finance, and Risk/Insurance.
  • Condition and Claims: Own transport-incident investigation and transport claims tracking. Secure pickup, delivery, and overage, shortage, and damage evidence; issue notices within applicable deadlines. Coordinate recovery with Legal and Risk/Insurance and obtain designated approval for settlements, salvage, or disposal.
  • Cost and Records: Validate quotes and invoices against approved rates, services, and evidence; provide commitments, accrual inputs, and forecasts to Finance. Maintain transport milestones, provider assignments, costs, exceptions, and evidence in the approved OFCI register with the Control Tower.
  • Handoffs and Reverse Logistics: Provide transport evidence to Inventory, Storage and Site Logistics for the consolidated custody and logistics handoff record. Coordinate returns, repairs, replacements, and inter-project transfers after disposition and commercial approvals. Construction retains site control and receiving acknowledgment.

title: Loss Prevention Officer
description:
Overview

Protect the Resort. Support the Team. Create a Safe Environment.

At Town and Country Resort, creating a welcoming and safe environment is everyone's responsibility. As a Loss Prevention Officer, you will help protect our Team Members, guests, property, and assets while ensuring our resort remains a safe, secure, and enjoyable destination.

This role is about more than security. It requires sound judgment, attention to detail, professionalism, and the ability to respond calmly to a variety of situations in a busy, 24-hour resort environment.

Why Town and Country Resort?

We are a San Diego landmark with a fresh perspective, a lively resort atmosphere, and a team that takes pride in creating memorable experiences. From conventions and celebrations to family getaways and everyday resort life, there is always something happening here.

Join a team where your awareness, professionalism, and commitment to safety make a meaningful difference every day.

Ready to help keep the resort safe? We’d love to meet you. Starting rates $21.50 - $22.50 based on shift. #towncountrySD

Responsibilities

What You Will Do

Safety and Security

  • Patrol resort grounds, guest areas, meeting spaces, parking areas, and back-of-house locations to promote a safe environment.

  • Monitor surveillance systems and access points, identifying and reporting suspicious activity or potential security concerns.

  • Respond promptly to emergencies, alarms, disturbances, and requests for assistance.

  • Conduct safety checks and report hazards, suspicious conditions, and security vulnerabilities.

  • Assist with emergency evacuations, medical incidents, fire alarms, and other emergency procedures.

Loss Prevention and Investigations

  • Help protect resort assets, equipment, supplies, and guest and Team Member property from loss, damage, or theft.

  • Document incidents, accidents, and security concerns accurately and objectively.

  • Assist with internal investigations involving missing property, theft, policy violations, and other reported concerns.

  • Preserve relevant information, including surveillance footage and witness statements, in accordance with resort procedures.

  • Maintain confidentiality and share sensitive information only with authorized individuals.

Guest and Team Member Support

  • Provide a visible, approachable security presence throughout the resort.

  • Assist guests and Team Members with safety concerns, directions, and requests for assistance.

  • Respond professionally to disputes and disruptive behavior, using de-escalation techniques whenever possible.

  • Enforce resort policies consistently, respectfully, and without unnecessary confrontation.

  • Work closely with Front Office, Housekeeping, Engineering, Food and Beverage, and resort leadership.

Communication and Documentation

  • Prepare detailed incident reports before the end of the shift or as otherwise directed.

  • Communicate important security issues and ongoing concerns during shift changes.

  • Maintain accurate records of lost and found property, key control, access issues, and other assigned security functions.

  • Follow established procedures for evidence handling, incident escalation, and emergency response.

Qualifications

What You Bring

  • Previous experience in security, loss prevention, hospitality, or a related field preferred.

  • Strong observation, communication, and problem-solving skills.

  • The ability to remain calm, professional, and objective during challenging situations.

  • Good judgment and the ability to recognize when to respond independently and when to contact a supervisor or emergency services.

  • Comfort using computers, radios, surveillance systems, and incident-reporting software.

  • A commitment to protecting confidential information and treating everyone with respect.

  • Flexibility to work a variety of shifts, including evenings, overnight shifts, weekends, and holidays.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to walk and patrol the resort for extended periods.

  • Ability to stand, climb stairs, and navigate indoor and outdoor areas, including parking lots and event spaces.

  • Ability to respond promptly to incidents and assist with emergency procedures.

  • Ability to lift and carry equipment or other items as reasonably required for the position, with or without reasonable accommodation.

Important Qualifications

  • Must meet applicable California requirements for the position, including any required security guard registration and training.

  • A valid California driver's license may be required if driving is an assigned responsibility.

  • Must successfully complete applicable pre-employment requirements.

Why Town and Country Resort?

Town and Country Resort is a San Diego landmark in Mission Valley, featuring 671 guest rooms, extensive meeting and event space, multiple dining venues, and a lively resort atmosphere. Our Loss Prevention team plays an important role in protecting the people, experiences, and property that make our resort special.

Interested in being part of the team that keeps our resort safe? We would like to meet you.

title: APP - St. Francis Urgent Care - PRN

description:
The Nurse Practitioner Non Exempt examines and treats patients independently and in autonomous collaboration with other health care professionals following established standards and practices. Ensures proper illness and injury care and disease prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and recovery. Relies on education, experience, professional training and judgement to accomplish responsibilities. A wide degree of creativity and latitude is expected. Works under minimal supervision under the direction of the collaborating physician, as appropriate. May lead and direct the work of others within scope of practice.

1. Patient Care: This will have been satisfactorily performed when…

  1. Patient assessment and teaching and learning needs are accurately documented, detailed nursing history is obtained, and patients at physiologic and or psychological risk are identified as evidenced by physical assessments of patients that identify priority care needs.
  2. Diagnosis is appropriately formulated with pertinent therapeutic and diagnostic procedures ordered at all times as evidenced by necessary procedures that are performed to implement plan of care based on care standards and, or protocols.
  3. Treatment plan is implemented with consults and referrals with interdisciplinary team regarding patient assessment findings conducted as appropriate at all times.
  4. Plan of care is reassessed, revised and modified based on physiological and psychosocial findings as evidenced by documentation in the treatment plan. Patient plan of care is reviewed with interdisciplinary team at all times.
  5. Tests and consults are ordered as required by plan of care, reviews test results 100% of the time. Plan of care is discussed with patient and family at all times as evidenced by documentation.
  6. Education is provided to patients based upon identified risk factors as evidenced by patient education programs that are developed, revised and evaluated based on the effectiveness of learning.

2. Partnership and Collaboration: This will have been satisfactorily performed when…

  1. All patient care activities are accurately documented as per documentation standards as evidenced by documentation of age appropriate, health education and community resource utilization being noted in records. Outcomes of documentation are evaluated and contributes to performance improvement initiatives through medical record review.
  2. Multidisciplinary teams are utilized appropriately as evidenced by collaboration with the interdisciplinary team and incorporation of the expertise of the interdisciplinary team to achieve patient outcomes 100% of the time.
  3. Students are precepted in accordance to specified guidelines.
  4. Patient care activities are efficiently coordinated, and communication facilitated to maximize patient outcomes at all times and ensure continuity of care.
  5. As a primary resource to patient care team, identifies, provides, develops and maintains learning resources for patient care team as requested.

3. Quality: This will have been satisfactorily performed when…

  1. Patient documentation is accurate and legible based on focused chart reviews 100% of the time.
  2. Safe therapeutic care is provided in holistic and systematic way to facilitate patients' achievement of desired outcomes at all times.
  3. Trends in patient populations are recognized, alternatives to care are explored and assistance is provided in the revision of standards, guidelines and or protocols as needed.
  4. Participation in clinical research is provided and current nursing research literature is reviewed as evidenced by demonstrated application to clinical practice.
  5. Practices that contribute to variance are analyzed, conclusions are drawn from aggregate data, resources to assist in variance analysis are identified and assistance with drawing conclusions from aggregate data is provided as evidenced by improved performance evidenced by outcomes.
  6. Assistance is provided in the development and revision of standards for patient populations incorporating a interdisciplinary approach and utilizing best practices and research findings.

4. Other Duties as Assigned: This will have been satisfactorily performed when…

  1. Other duties as assigned are completed within specified time frames.
  2. Actively participates in hospital committees and other quality improvement activities as requested by manager.

Experience
None


Education
See licensure requirements


Training
See licensure requirements.


Special Skills
Customer Service, Verbal and Communication, Computer Skills


Licensure
Advanced Practice License from Louisiana State Board of Nursing and Certification as Nurse Practitioner by ANCC or AANP and Current Louisiana state RN license and Current BLS Certification (within 6 months of hire)

As a Systems Administrator at ACI, you will maintain and support operating system environments and computer systems across multiple domains, administer Windows and Linux systems, support secure architectures, and collaborate with engineering teams to meet system and application requirements.

title: Project Coordinator, Europe
description:
Revolution Medicines is a global, commercial-state oncology company dedicated to discovering, developing and delivering innovative medicines for patients with RAS-addicted cancers. Leveraging its differentiated RAS(ON) tri-complex inhibitor platform, the company is advancing a broad, integrated portfolio of oral RAS(ON) inhibitors designed to directly target the active, cancer-driving state of RAS. Founded on rigorous scientific inquiry and a willingness to challenge long-held assumptions, Revolution Medicines is committed to changing the trajectory of disease for patients with RAS-addicted cancers worldwide.

Our people are united by a shared way of working: follow the science, challenge assumptions, act with urgency and hold ourselves to a high standard of rigor—all in service of patients.

The Opportunity

The Project Coordinator serves as a trusted administrative partner to the Vice President (VP), Medical Affairs and the European SWAT team, comprising Medical, Market Access, and Commercial. Reporting to the VP, Medical Affairs, this role provides executive support and coordinates day-to-day administrative activities across the three functions to enhance team effectiveness and support collaboration across Europe.

The role also partners with administrative colleagues across Europe and globally to establish consistent ways of working and coordinate support for the SWAT team across the European markets.

The successful candidate will thrive in a fast-paced environment, exercise independent and sound judgment, build strong partnerships across the organization, and establish reliable administrative processes that support the team as it grows.

Key responsibilities include

As the lead administrative support to the VP, Medical Affairs and the European SWAT team, this role enables leadership and team effectiveness through proactive coordination, executive support, and cross-functional collaboration.

  • Manage the VP’s complex global calendar and coordinate SWAT team scheduling, balancing competing priorities, proactively resolving scheduling conflicts, and ensuring readiness for meetings across global time zones.

  • Coordinate engagement across the SWAT team and European markets by partnering with administrative colleagues and cross-functional stakeholders to optimize scheduling and meeting effectiveness.

  • Coordinate travel for the VP and SWAT team, including itineraries and bookings, and organize team meetings, off-sites, and events, including logistics, follow-up, and action item tracking.

  • Prepare meeting agendas, compile and distribute materials, record minutes and decisions, and follow up with action owners on agreed deadlines.

  • Provide administrative coordination for SWAT team projects, maintaining timelines, action trackers, and status updates and escalating overdue items to the relevant team members.

  • Draft routine correspondence and format presentations, reports, and briefing documents using content provided by the VP and SWAT team; coordinate document review and distribution.

  • Coordinate the administrative processing of consulting agreements, statements of work, purchase requests, and vendor engagements supporting SWAT team activities, in partnership with Legal, Procurement, and Finance; track approvals, signatures, and renewals.

  • Maintain trackers for purchase orders, invoices, and team activity expenditure; follow up on payment queries and provide administrative support to budget owners and Finance.

  • Build trusted partnerships across the organization while handling sensitive information with the highest level of confidentiality and discretion.

  • Maintain shared team files, contact lists, distribution lists, and administrative records, ensuring documents are current, organized, and accessible to authorized colleagues.

  • Partner with country administrative colleagues and SWAT team members to develop, implement, and continuously improve administrative workflows, templates, and coordination practices.

  • Support the administrative onboarding and integration of SWAT team members by coordinating induction meetings, preparing team information packs, and maintaining onboarding checklists with HR and the relevant managers.

  • Share administrative tools and best practices with European and global administrative colleagues and coordinate backup support when needed.

  • Participate in the corporate administrative community, build strong partnerships and advance collaboration across administrative teams.

Required Skills, Experience and Education:

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and experience.

  • 8+ years of progressively responsible experience providing executive support to senior leaders and administrative support to cross-functional teams within a fast-paced environment.

  • Experience supporting senior executives and leadership teams within a matrixed regional organization, including complex regional calendar management, travel planning, and meeting coordination.

  • Experience coordinating administrative support across multiple functions, managing competing requests, and agreeing priorities with senior leaders.

  • Demonstrated ability to independently manage multiple competing priorities, exercise sound judgment and discretion, anticipate needs, identify risks, and proactively implement solutions.

  • Exceptional organizational, administrative coordination, and time management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to follow through on actions and deadlines across functions.

  • Strong business acumen, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to build productive relationships across functions, levels, and external partners.

  • Able to handle highly confidential information with professionalism, integrity, and discretion.

  • Proactive, solution-oriented mindset with the flexibility to thrive in a dynamic, high-growth environment.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite, including Outlook, PowerPoint, Word, Teams, and Excel.

Preferred Skills:

  • Biotechnology, pharmaceutical, or life sciences industry experience.

  • Experience supporting a growing regional team across Medical Affairs, Market Access, and Commercial.

  • Experience with contract administration, procurement processes, expense reporting, invoice processing, and budget tracking.

  • Familiarity with project management tools such as Smartsheet, Asana, or similar platforms.

title: Team Lead, Market Operations - Des Moines, IA
description:
About Carvana

At Carvana, we sell cars, but we are not salespeople. We have made it our mission to create a hassle-free way for people to buy and sell cars. We saw a huge problem with how much of a headache it is to buy a car the traditional way, so we committed ourselves to put customer satisfaction at the core of our business, we have built a no-pressure, no-haggle online car buying experience that saves our customers time and money. Customers can search through thousands of vehicles online, see full 360-degree views of both the interior and exterior of the vehicles before deciding to go through the purchasing process. Our Customer Advocates will then either deliver the purchased vehicle to our customer’s driveway using one of our kick-ass one car haulers, or they will meet our customers at one of our amazing coin-operated Vending Machines.

For more information on Carvana and our mission, sneak a peek at our company introduction video.

About the team and position

Carvana’s Market Operation department is known for its team-oriented, fast-paced environment. We hire bright people who are willing to roll up their sleeves, step in wherever needed, mentor and develop team members, and assume additional responsibilities as needed while juggling multiple projects. Don’t forget to bring your personality! We thrive from each unique perspective. Our strength is in our diversity of opinions.

Job Description

The Team Lead, in our Market Operations group, is responsible for running the local Carvana hub and everything that comes with it, including (but not limited to); market launch, operations, logistics, consumer branding, team engagement and effectiveness and, of course, the market’s ongoing success. We are looking for someone who is a big picture thinker with the ability to manage the employee and customer experience. A Team Lead not only crushes daily operations, but they have the savvy to assess business trends and proactively create solutions to potential roadblocks. We need a strong people leader, as a Team Lead works closely with a team of extremely talented Customer Advocates and is responsible for providing vision and development opportunities.

What you’ll be Doing

  • Be a continuous positive force within the market and create strong morale and spirit throughout the team.
  • Help interview, select, onboard and train a team of Customer Advocates and provide the tools, resources and guidance they need to be successful. Employee development is an essential part of this role.
  • Actively develop a team of Customer Advocates by providing feedback, conducting performance check-ins, and setting goals to improve performance and skill set.
  • Recognize and reinforce individual and team accomplishments by using existing organizational tools and programs as well as by finding new, creative and effective methods of recognition.
  • Generate and monitor regular reports like a boss and presenting to upper management… also like a boss.
  • Be the go to expert for your team. You’re always ready to jump in alongside an Advocate to wash cars or jump into our kick-ass single-car hauler and deliver cars to our customers while providing a stellar customer experience.
