title: Supply Chain Analytics Intern [Winter 2027]
description:
Figure is an AI robotics company developing autonomous general-purpose humanoid robots. The goal of the company is to ship humanoid robots with human level intelligence. Its robots are engineered to perform a variety of tasks in the home and commercial markets. Figure is headquartered in San Jose, CA.

We are looking for a Supply Chain Analytics Intern to join our Global Supply Management (GSM) team. In summary, you will own the GSM team's supplier ramp and sourcing readiness toolset as we move from one prototype build to the next, and at the end of your term run the build kickoff readiness review off it.

Responsibilities:

  • Own the sourcing status tracker: one record per part on the current and next build bills of materials showing awarded supplier, quote status, NDA and master supply agreement (MSA) status, and approved supplier list (ASL) qualification status. Refresh it weekly so GSMs and program management can see which parts have no supplier on paper.
  • Own the tooling and non-recurring engineering (NRE) tracker: every GSM-owned tooling and NRE purchase orders, with kickoff, T1 sample, first article inspection (FAI), and payment milestone dates tracked against need dates.
  • Own the build cost baseline and next-build cost targets: normalize quotes across suppliers, roll them up by sub-assembly for the current build, then set targets by sub-assembly for the next build. This becomes the baseline for the team's cost reduction tracking through future builds.
  • Own the supplier capacity view: committed supplier capacity against the next-build forecast by part and by source, flagging where a supplier cannot meet demand before build kickoff. Support onboarding of new vendors by collecting NDA, MSA, and quality documents for GSM review.
  • Pull supplier scorecard data for the GSM-run quarterly business reviews (QBRs) and build quote analysis packages that GSMs take into negotiations.
  • At the end of the term, run the build kickoff readiness review off your toolset and document the handoff so the team can run it without you.

Requirements:

  • Rising senior or recent graduate in Supply Chain Management, Industrial Engineering, Operations, Business, or a related field; must be graduating within one year
  • Available full time for the winter term, January through April 2027 (approximately 16 weeks)
  • Advanced Excel (Power Query, lookups, pivots) and at least one of SQL or Python for pulling and joining data across systems
  • Working knowledge of hardware supply chain basics: bills of materials, supplier quotes, purchase orders, and tooling
  • Clear written communication; able to document a process so someone else can run it

Bonus Qualifications:

  • Prior internship or co-op in sourcing, procurement, or supply chain at a hardware company
  • Hands-on experience with an ERP (NetSuite preferred) or a BI tool such as Power BI or Tableau
  • Exposure to should-cost analysis, quote normalization, or cost reduction tracking on a physical product

The US base salary range for this full-time position is between $35 - $40/hr.

The pay offered for this position may vary based on several individual factors, including job-related knowledge, skills, and experience. The total compensation package may also include additional components/benefits depending on the specific role. This information will be shared if an employment offer is extended.

title: Senior Build Reliability Engineer
description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

The Senior Build Reliability Engineer partners closely with the design and manufacturing teams to right-size processes and controls to enable scaling the production of spacecraft hardware. Build Reliability Engineers ensure production processes yield verified, reliable hardware at rate. You will flex beyond Build Reliability to support Quality, Flight Reliability, and Mission Assurance. The ideal candidate is a responsible, collaborative, process-oriented engineer with hands-on hardware design/test/manufacturing/troubleshooting experience.

Responsibilities

  • Partner with design engineering and manufacturing teams to create test, manufacturability, and inspection plans for all vehicle hardware.
  • Contain suspect or known non-conforming product, providing guidance to quality inspectors, technicians, shop supervisors, and engineers.
  • Lead failure investigations in production, test, and operation; identifying and mitigating immediate and underlying root causes to reduce risk and improve the reliability of designs and processes.
  • Provide critical peer review of hardware during design reviews and acceptance and qualification test campaigns.
  • Perform failure modes and effects analyses, build requirements compliance matrix tools, and ensure adequate test coverage, change management, and manufacturability of flight hardware.
  • Own vehicle level deliverables for regulatory bodies including requirements compliance, functional or flight hazard analyses, and verification evidence.
  • Support Mission Assurance's vehicle level risk management and identification/tracking/execution of mitigations.

Basic Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in aerospace, computer science, electrical, manufacturing, mechanical, or material sciences engineering.
  • 5+ years professional experience in aerospace, design, quality, or related engineering role.
  • Hands-on hardware test, qualification, troubleshooting, or failure analysis experience.
  • Commitment to lean quality principles without compromising safety or reliability.
  • Demonstrated application of process controls in high volume manufacturing, test, and quality environments.
  • Experience generating, processing, and/or analyzing data for production insight.
  • Strong interpersonal and collaborative skills, with a drive to innovate and improve reliability in cutting-edge technology.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Full project lifecycle ownership experience (cradle-to-grave).
  • Proficiency with quality tools such as measurement systems analysis, design of experiments, statistical process control, root cause analysis and corrective action, advanced product quality planning (APQP), metrology, process failure mode and effects analysis (PFMEA), control plans, and various problem-solving approaches.
  • Hands-on knowledge of CNC machining, additive manufacturing, casting, welding, fastening, or other special manufacturing processes.

Pay Range

  • Salary range: Senior: $140,333 - $179,314/ per year.
  • This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA.
  • Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance.
  • You will be eligible for incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards.

Benefits

Consider your benefits covered for launch. At Varda, we invest in benefits and perks that support your health, financial well-being, and life beyond work. Benefits vary by position, with packages designed specifically for our regular full-time employees and interns.

Regular Full-Time Positions:

  • Flexible PTO policy + 12 paid holidays
  • 100% company-paid Medical, Dental, and Vision insurance plans for employees and dependents with FSA and employer-matched HSA options
  • Voluntary accident, hospital, critical illness, and pet insurance
  • $120/month wellness reimbursement for gym and fitness expenses
  • 12 weeks of parental leave (with supplemental disability leave for CA mothers)
  • Family building, pregnancy, parenting and menopause benefits via Maven Clinic
  • Sponsored One Medical memberships for employees and their dependents

Workplace Experience & Perks

title: Loss Prevention Supervisor
description:
Overview

Town and Country Resort | San Diego, CA

Town and Country Resort is looking for a Loss Prevention Supervisor to help create a safe, secure, and welcoming environment for our Team Members, guests, and property.

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is comfortable being visible throughout the resort, responding to incidents, supporting the Loss Prevention team, and working closely with hotel leadership and other departments. Starting rate $25 per hour. #towncountrySD

Responsibilities

What You'll Do

  • Supervise and support Loss Prevention Officers during assigned shifts.
  • Maintain a visible presence throughout the resort, including guest areas, back-of-house areas, parking areas, and meeting spaces.
  • Respond promptly and professionally to guest, Team Member, and property-related incidents.
  • Conduct and document investigations involving theft, property damage, safety concerns, accidents, disturbances, and other incidents.
  • Prepare accurate and timely incident reports and maintain appropriate documentation.
  • Monitor security systems, access points, CCTV, alarms, and other Loss Prevention equipment.
  • Assist with emergency response procedures, including fire/life safety situations and other emergencies.
  • Work closely with hotel leadership, People Services, Engineering, Front Office, Housekeeping, and other departments when security or safety concerns arise.
  • Assist with investigations involving Team Members while maintaining appropriate confidentiality.
  • Monitor resort activity and identify potential safety, security, or loss-prevention concerns.
  • Support the implementation and enforcement of resort safety and security procedures.
  • Assist with training Loss Prevention Officers and other Team Members on safety, security, and emergency procedures.
  • Provide direction and support during large meetings, conventions, special events, and high-occupancy periods.
  • Conduct regular patrols and security checks of the property.
  • Respond appropriately to situations involving disruptive behavior, unauthorized access, suspicious activity, or other potential threats.
  • Complete shift logs, reports, inspections, and other required documentation.
  • Perform other duties as assigned.

Qualifications

What We're Looking For

  • Previous experience in hotel security, loss prevention, public safety, or a related field.
  • Previous supervisory or leadership experience preferred.
  • Strong observation, communication, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to remain calm and professional during emergencies or challenging situations.
  • Good judgment and the ability to handle sensitive information appropriately.
  • Ability to write clear, accurate, and objective reports.
  • Comfortable interacting with guests, Team Members, leaders, vendors, and emergency personnel.
  • Ability to work independently while also functioning as part of a team.
  • Ability to prioritize multiple situations in a busy resort environment.
  • Basic computer skills and the ability to learn security and hotel systems.
  • CPR/First Aid certification or the ability to obtain certification is preferred.
  • Ability to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, holidays, and overnight shifts as needed.

Physical Requirements

This position requires regular walking and standing throughout the resort and may require responding quickly to different areas of the property. The position may also involve sitting, bending, reaching, climbing stairs, and occasionally assisting with emergency situations.

Why Join Town and Country?

At Town and Country Resort, no two days are exactly alike. Our 671-room resort, extensive meeting and event space, restaurants, bars, pools, and year-round activity create an environment where Loss Prevention plays an important role in keeping the entire property running safely and smoothly.

If you are someone who pays attention to the details, stays calm under pressure, and enjoys being part of a team, we'd like to meet you.

Come grow your career at Town and Country Resort.

title: Prediction Markets Operations Intern (Winter 2027)
description:
About the Company

Gemini is a global crypto and Web3 platform founded by Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss in 2014, offering a wide range of simple, reliable, and secure crypto products and services to individuals and institutions in over 70 countries. Our mission is to unlock the next era of financial, creative, and personal freedom by providing trusted access to the decentralized future. We envision a world where crypto reshapes the global financial system, internet, and money to create greater choice, independence, and opportunity for all — bridging traditional finance with the emerging cryptoeconomy in a way that is more open, fair, and secure. As a publicly traded company, Gemini is poised to accelerate this vision with greater scale, reach, and impact.

The Department: Marketing

The Prediction Markets Operations team turns real-world events into clearly defined event contracts. We support markets across their full lifecycle—from an initial idea, through configuration and launch, into live operations, and finally to accurate resolution. Our work sits at the intersection of current events, marketplaces, and regulated products, and it demands precision at every step.

The team is responsible for making sure every contract is: clearly and objectively written, based on reliable, authoritative resolution sources, accurately configured, supported with appropriate images and content, thoroughly reviewed before launch, monitored while live, and resolved accurately and consistently.

The Role: Prediction Markets Operations Intern

This is a detail-oriented, hands-on internship for someone interested in marketplaces, operations, current events, financial technology, or regulated products. You will perform time-sensitive operational work and learn firsthand how prediction markets move from an idea to a live and, ultimately, settled contract.

Success in this role depends on accuracy, sound judgment, reliability, and operational discipline. Just as important is the willingness to escalate uncertainty rather than guess. You will support, coordinate, research, prepare, review, and execute work under established procedures, working closely with partners across Prediction Markets, Operations, Customer Support, Product, Engineering, Compliance, Legal, Design, Marketing, and our liquidity partners.

This will be a semester long internship program with 3 days a week in person at our New York City, NY office from January to April 2027.

Responsibilities:

Contract Research and Market Listings

  • Research potential prediction-market contract ideas.
  • Help turn ideas into precise, objective binary questions.
  • Identify reliable and authoritative public resolution sources.
  • Flag ambiguity, potentially prohibited subject matter, or questions requiring Compliance or Legal review.
  • Prepare contract specifications, including outcomes, dates, descriptions, tickers, resolution criteria, and other listing details.
  • Create and configure event contracts in the Contract Management System, or assist with structured CSV uploads, under established procedures.
  • Support research and documentation related to product requirements and filings.

Quality Assurance and Launch Operations

  • Perform pre-launch and post-upload quality assurance.
  • Verify contract names, outcomes, ordering, start times, expiration times, resolution criteria, and designated sources.
  • Review dates and times carefully, including UTC-based fields.
  • Compare contracts with relevant external prediction markets when appropriate, and identify unintended differences in outcomes, timing, or mechanics.
  • Confirm that event and social images are present and appropriate.
  • Upload or update approved event images, social images, and display settings.
  • Coordinate launch information with internal stakeholders and liquidity partners.
  • Identify discrepancies and escalate issues before launch.

Customer and Live-Market Support

  • Review, triage, and investigate prediction-market support tickets.
  • Gather relevant facts, document findings, and route issues appropriately.
  • Monitor live markets for incorrect content, timing discrepancies, operational issues, or unexpected behavior.
  • Follow established incident-escalation procedures when urgent technical or operational issues arise.
  • Maintain accurate trackers, checklists, SOPs, and internal documentation.
  • Identify opportunities to improve repetitive workflows and reduce manual work.

Market Monitoring and Resolution

  • Monitor contracts approaching expiration or awaiting resolution.
  • Research outcomes using the contract’s designated resolution source.
  • Prepare a proposed outcome, source links, and a concise rationale for internal review.
  • Double-check resolution information against authoritative sources.
  • Escalate unclear, conflicting, delayed, or incomplete source information rather than guessing.
  • Execute approved market settlements in the Contract Management System after required training, review, and approval.
    • Settlement activity is performed only under established procedures, supervision, access controls, and approval requirements. Accuracy is critical, because completed settlements may not be reversible.
  • Document completed resolutions according to team procedures.

Scheduled Monitoring Coverage

  • Participate in a scheduled rotation for brief evening or weekend monitoring.
  • This is lightweight, scheduled coverage—not continuous or unrestricted on-call work.
  • Interns will primarily identify and escalate issues to the appropriate full-time team.

Minimum Qualifications:

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s, Associate’s, or Master’s degree.
  • Exceptional attention to detail.
  • Strong written communication.
  • Ability to research information and distinguish authoritative sources from unreliable ones.
  • Sound judgment and a willingness to escalate uncertainty.
  • Comfort with detailed, repeatable, process-driven tasks.
  • Ability to manage time-sensitive work without sacrificing accuracy.
  • Dependability and follow-through.
  • Basic proficiency with spreadsheets and web-based business tools.
  • Ability to work in-office.
  • Availability for the scheduled, lightweight evening or weekend monitoring rotation.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Internship, academic, or project experience in operations, customer support, research, quality assurance, content operations, marketplaces, fintech, or another detail-oriented environment.
  • Familiarity with prediction markets, financial markets, sports, politics, economics, or major current events.
  • Experience with ticketing platforms, content-management systems, administrative tools, dashboards, or structured data entry.
  • Interest in regulated products or operational risk.
  • Experience creating or maintaining process documentation.
  • Comfort learning unfamiliar internal tools quick.

Pay Rate: The hourly pay rate for this role is $40/hour in the State of New York. When determining a candidate’s compensation, we consider a number of factors including skillset, experience, job scope, and current market data.

In the United States, we offer a hybrid work approach at our hub offices, balancing the benefits of in-person collaboration with the flexibility of remote work. Expectations may vary by location and role, so candidates are encouraged to connect with their recruiter to learn more about the specific policy for the role. Employees who do not live near one of our hubs are part of our remote workforce. All employees, however, are required to onboard in-person at one of our office locations.

At Gemini, we strive to build diverse teams that reflect the people we want to empower through our products, and we are committed to equal employment opportunity regardless of race, color, ancestry, religion, sex, national origin, sexual orientation, age, citizenship, marital status, disability, gender identity, or Veteran status. Equal Opportunity is the Law, and Gemini is proud to be an equal opportunity workplace. If you have a specific need that requires accommodation, please let a member of the People Team know.

title: Staff Software Engineer, Government Programs
description:
About the role

Muon is looking for a Staff Software Engineer to join our team and help scale our core platforms. In this role, you'll have high-level, organizational impact designing foundational architecture, developing shared libraries and services, and developing technical strategies to ship customer-facing features with real, immediate impact. This role will be a technical lead, building the platforms that enable Muon's missions for our government programs.

You'll work within a tight-knit team that values open communication, cross-functional collaboration, and moving quickly without cutting corners. You'll partner closely with other engineering teams to translate business needs into reliable, well-crafted solutions. Whether you're building something from scratch or improving what already exists, you'll have a direct hand in shaping the systems our customers depend on every day. This will include developing software and infrastructure in classified environments.

Responsibilities

  • Design, build, and evolve high-performance systems that are scalable, resilient, and reliable in regulated environments
  • Deploy, operate, and maintain software platforms and infrastructure into classified environments, including meeting relevant security, compliance, and accreditation requirements.
  • Ensure execution across interdependent, multi-month epics and initiatives.
  • Own architectural decisions that shape the long-term direction of our core systems.
  • Define metrics aligned with critical company goals
  • Identify and resolve bottlenecks, performance issues, and systemic risks in production environments.
  • Partner with cross-functional teams to translate business and product needs into well-crafted technical solutions.
  • Mentor teams and senior engineers, define training plans, define standards for code, testing, design and review.

title: Mechanical Simulation Engineer
description:
About SK hynix America:

At SK hynix America, we are at the forefront of semiconductor innovation. As a global leader in HBM, DRAM, and NAND flash technologies, we develop the advanced memory solutions powering everything from advanced mobile technology to massive AI data centers. With major investments in the U.S. and a leading position in the global AI revolution, we build the critical infrastructure of the digital landscape and remain committed to sustainable operations. We invite innovative minds to be part of our journey. Here, you will be part of a collaborative team pioneering the next generation of memory technologies, expanding our market footprint, and defining the future of computing.

Work Model: Onsite

Job Overview:

SK hynix America is seeking a highly skilled and motivated Mechanical Simulation Engineer to join our Advanced Packaging (PKG) R&D team. In this role, you will be at the forefront of semiconductor innovation, driving the mechanical integrity of next-generation packaging solutions (e.g., HBM, 2.5D/3D Heterogeneous Integration). You will utilize advanced numerical methods to predict and optimize the thermos-mechanical behavior of complex IC packages, ensuring high performance and structural robustness. Additionally, you will bridge the gap between package-level integrity and system-level performance, ensuring our packaging solutions are robustly integrated into data center rack architectures and consumer systems.

Responsibilities:

  • Advanced FEA Modeling: Develop high-fidelity, non-linear Finite Element Analysis (FEA) models to characterize stress, strain, and warpage behavior in advanced semiconductor packages during assembly processes and reliability tests.
  • Multi-Physics Analysis: Perform complex thermo-mechanical multi-physics simulations to evaluate the impact of thermal gradients on structural integrity and fatigue life.
  • Design Optimization: Partner closely with package designers and process engineers to provide simulation-driven design directions, optimizing architectures for warpage control, solder joint reliability, and interfacial adhesion.
  • Material Characterization: Define and implement material constitutive models (elastic, plastic, viscoelastic, etc.) for various packaging materials (EMC, Substrate, Silicon, TIM) and correlate simulation results with empirical data (e.g., Shadow Moire, DIC).
  • Failure Analysis & Reliability: Predict potential failure modes (delamination, cracking, bump fatigue) and develop mitigation strategies to meet stringent industry reliability standards.
  • Methodology Development: Establish and document standardized simulation workflows, advanced meshing techniques, and automation scripts to enhance simulation accuracy and throughput.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Present technical findings and simulation-based risks to internal stakeholders and global R&D teams to influence product roadmaps and manufacturing process specs.
  • System-Level Interaction Analysis: Evaluate the thermo-mechanical interactions between advanced packages and board/system-level components (e.g., Motherboard, Rack, Cooling systems), mapping system-level boundary conditions down to the package level.

Qualifications:

  • Master’s degree or higher in Mechanical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field. Candidates with relevant industry experience are preferred
  • Core Expertise: Deep understanding of solid mechanics, heat transfer, and strength of materials, specifically applied to semiconductor packaging.
  • Simulation Tools: Extensive experience with commercial FEA software such as ABAQUS (preferred), ANSYS Mechanical, or LS-DYNA.
  • Technical Knowledge: Proven knowledge of semiconductor packaging structures (Flip-chip, WLCSP, 2.5D/3D IC) and the physics of failure in electronic assemblies.
  • Analytical Skills: Ability to interpret complex simulation data and translate it into actionable engineering recommendations.
  • System-Level Insight: Experience or strong knowledge in mechanical simulation/testing at the system or set level, with preferred exposure to data center rack architectures, desktop form factors, or enterprise-level hardware systems.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Experience in Multi-scale modeling (from micro-scale TSV/micro Bumps to macro-scale Package/PCB).
  • Strong scripting skills in Python to automate Abaqus workflows, including pre-processing, job submission, and customized post-processing/data extraction.
  • Proficiency in statistical analysis and DOE (Design of Experiments) using tools such as JMP or Minitab to interpret simulation and experiment data.
  • Knowledge of semiconductor manufacturing processes (Reflow, Molding, Bonding) and their impact on residual stress.
  • Experience with CAD software (NX, Solidworks, or AutoCAD) for geometry preparation and cleaning.
  • Excellent communication skills to collaborate effectively within a multidisciplinary, global R&D environment.

Benefits:

  • Top Tier health insurance at no employee cost
  • Paid day offs: Paid Time Off, Company Holidays, Parental Leave, Happy Fridays
  • 401k Matching
  • Flexible Spending Account (FSA) for Health Care & Dependent Care
  • Educational reimbursement up to $10,000 per year
  • Donation Matching and volunteering opportunities
  • Corporate discount programs
  • Free Breakfast/Lunch/Dinner provided to employees

About This Role

The Build Reliability Engineer II partners closely with the design and manufacturing teams to right-size processes and controls to enable scaling the production of spacecraft hardware. Build Reliability Engineers ensure production processes yield verified, reliable hardware at rate. You will flex beyond Build Reliability to support Quality, Flight Reliability, and Mission Assurance.   • Experience generating, processing, and/or analyzing data for production insight.

title: Principal AI Platform Engineer
description:
• Great opportunity to add significant value to Technology, AI & Transformation for the Qantas Group!
  • Permanent opportunity based at our Mascot office (hybrid working available)
  • Staff Travel Benefits from Day One

At Qantas, we represent Australia to the world. Our diverse country is known for its unique spirit, mateship, and a can-do attitude. Together we’re strong and resilient, and we work hard to make sure we’re always at our best.

As the Principal AI Platform Engineer you'll be part of the team building the AI platform that the rest of the Group builds on. That means treating the platform as a product and the engineers who use it as your customers: paved paths that make the right way the easy way, self-service onboarding, and guardrails and guidance instead of gatekeeping. Success is measured by adoption and by how rarely teams need you. Data scientists, ML engineers and application teams should be able to onboard, build, deploy and operate their own AI workloads in production without platform team intervention.

You'll be the senior technical voice in the squad. You'll own the technical design of the platform, set the engineering standards and patterns the team builds to, and lift the capability of the engineers around you through design review, pairing and mentoring. It's also a hands-on role: you'll be writing production code, building infrastructure as code and CI/CD pipelines, and operationalising the platform on AWS SageMaker and Bedrock, working alongside the team rather than directing delivery from a distance.

You'll make the platform secure, observable, reproducible and cost-transparent, so teams can see their own consumption and troubleshoot their own workloads, with responsible AI, privacy and security controls built in from the start rather than bolted on. You'll work in a small cross-functional squad led by a Product Owner, partnering with the AI Solution Architect, Cloud Engineer and AI Platform Engineers.

What you will bring:

  • 8+ years designing, building and operating scalable data and AI/ML platforms in large enterprise environments, including demonstrated technical leadership on complex platform initiatives
  • · Bachelor's degree or higher in computer science, software engineering, data science or a related field
  • Deep hands-on cloud-native engineering on AWS, including SageMaker, Bedrock, S3, IAM and related DevOps tooling, with Python, infrastructure as code (Terraform or CloudFormation) and CI/CD pipelines
  • Proven experience designing, implementing and managing secure, governed and cost-optimised AI/ML platforms, with a strong understanding of enterprise security, monitoring and access control frameworks
  • Experience establishing platform engineering practices and standards within an enterprise architecture and governance framework: defining patterns, creating reusable templates and building developer experience tooling
  • Hands-on production MLOps capability (pipelines, model registry, feature and artefact management, serving, monitoring) and GenAI capability (prompt engineering, LLM orchestration, RAG, evaluation, guardrails)
  • Platform as a product mindset: self-service, golden paths, guardrails over gatekeeping, and treating internal engineers as customers
  • Able to translate high-level architecture and product requirements into detailed technical designs, implementation plans and actionable backlog items
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, able to communicate highly technical information to non-technical stakeholders and influence without authority in a highly matrixed organisation
  • Track record of delivering complex technical initiatives with a high degree of autonomy, while mentoring and uplifting team capability, navigating ambiguity, shifting priorities and operational dependencies

Why Qantas?

You’ll join a team where creativity and passion are encouraged. Our people come together to allow us to dream big and deliver successfully.

There are many different opportunities across our team, which means you’ll be able to grow both personally and professionally at Qantas. Your development is a priority for us – so that you can maintain the high standards our customers have come to expect and can continue to develop over time. You’ll be supported from day 1 with on-the-job training and coaching as well as our formal training opportunities. While you may start in this role, we’ve got a great track record of supporting our people to take their career in so many different directions, the destinations are endless.

The Qantas employee benefits program offers amazing benefits that extend well beyond travel:

  • We love to travel: Enjoy heavily discounted air travel within Australia and across the globe, both for you and your family and friends, as well as exclusive deals on accommodation and holidays.
  • We have flexible leave options: Make use of leave and flexible working opportunities including 18 weeks paid parental leave (plus superannuation payments on all paid and unpaid parental leave until your child turns 1) and additional purchased leave options for eligible employees.
  • We’ll give you access to thousands of rewards: Through our partnerships we can offer you discounts across shopping, food and wine, insurance, health and wellbeing, leisure and entertainment. You can also take advantage of our salary packaging program including motor vehicles, eligible portable electronic devices and professional memberships.

· We’ll support your wellbeing: Whether it’s learning to better support your own and others’ mental health, our interactive wellbeing app or your very own tailored nutrition plan.

Qantas is an Equal Opportunity Employer, so by coming to work for us, you’ll be part of an organisation that encourages diversity, supports charities and environmental initiatives. We encourage Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander – and people from every other kind of background – to apply.

We are committed to creating an inclusive workplace. Talk to us about how this job could be flexible for you.

National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA)

The 2025 National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA), Section 3112, generally prohibits citizens of China, Russia, Iran and North Korea without dual US citizenship or legal permanent residence from accessing specific non-public areas of national security or nuclear weapons facilities. The restrictions of NDAA Section 3112 apply to this position. To be qualified for this position, Candidates must be eligible to access the Laboratory in compliance with Section 3112.

Pre-Employment Drug Test

External applicant(s) selected for this position must pass a post-offer, pre-employment drug test. This includes testing for use of marijuana as Federal Law applies to us as a Federal Contractor.

Wireless and Medical Devices

Per the Department of Energy (DOE), Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory must meet certain restrictions with the use and/or possession of mobile devices in Limited Areas. Depending on your job duties, you may be required to work in a Limited Area where you are not permitted to have a personal and/or laboratory mobile device in your possession. This includes, but not limited to cell phones, tablets, fitness devices, wireless headphones, and other Bluetooth/wireless enabled devices.

If you use a medical device, which pairs with a mobile device, you must still follow the rules concerning the mobile device in individual sections within Limited Areas. Sensitive Compartmented Information Facilities require separate approval. Hearing aids without wireless capabilities or wireless that has been disabled are allowed in Limited Areas, Secure Space and Transit/Buffer Space within buildings.

How to identify fake job advertisements

Please be aware of recruitment scams where people or entities are misusing the name of Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory (LLNL) to post fake job advertisements. LLNL never extends an offer without a personal interview and will never charge a fee for joining our company. All current job openings are displayed on the Career Page under “Find Your Job” of our website. If you have encountered a job posting or have been approached with a job offer that you suspect may be fraudulent, we strongly recommend you do not respond.

To learn more about recruitment scams:

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, marital status, national origin, ancestry, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, disability, medical condition, pregnancy, protected veteran status, age, citizenship, or any other characteristic protected by applicable laws.

California Privacy Notice

The California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) grants privacy rights to all California residents. The law also entitles job applicants, employees, and non-employee workers to be notified of what personal information LLNL collects and for what purpose. The Employee Privacy Notice can be accessed here.

Our mission spans four critical national security areas nuclear deterrence, threat preparedness, energy security, and multi-domain defense empowering teams to take on the toughest challenges of today and tomorrow. title: Lead Electrical Engineering Technician
description:
At Honeywell Aerospace Engineering Test Services (ETS), we develop test equipment that exercises our products across a variety of product lines. As a Sr. Electrical Engineering Technician, you will support engineering by assembling custom or commercial off‑the‑shelf (COTS) electronic equipment into standardized rack configurations, fabricating and routing cable harnesses, and performing electrical cabinet wiring, troubleshooting, and repairs. This role is hands‑on and ideal for someone with strong technical abilities, attention to detail, and experience working with electronic assemblies.

You will report to the Test Engineering Manager, and work out of our Tempe, AZ on an in-person work schedule.

Key Responsibilities

  • Assemble COTS electronic equipment and instrumentation into equipment racks according to engineering drawings and standards.
  • Perform point‑to‑point wiring inside electrical cabinets and enclosures following established wiring diagrams.
  • Ensure proper electrical connections, continuity, grounding, and labeling according to standards.
  • Build, route, and terminate cable harnesses.
  • Maintain an organized, clean workspace and comply with all site safety, ESD, and tool‑control rules.

Physical Requirements

  • Ability to sit, stand, bend, reach, and use hands for electronic assembly, testing, and troubleshooting tasks.
  • Manual dexterity and hand-eye coordination to work with small components, tools, and wiring.
  • Ability to lift and move materials and equipment up to 25 pounds, with heavier items moved using assistance or appropriate equipment.
  • Ability to use test equipment, computers, and read detailed technical documentation.
  • Ability to wear required PPE and perform duties safely in a laboratory or production environment, with or without reasonable accommodation.

YOU MUST HAVE

  • Minimum 4 years of experience in electrical technical support or related roles.
  • Experience interpreting electrical schematics, wiring diagrams, bills of materials.
  • Skilled with crimping, soldering, cable routing, wire labeling, and use of standard electrical tools/meters.

WE VALUE

  • Technical degree, military training, or equivalent hands‑on experience in electrical/electronic systems.
  • Familiarity with IPC 620 preferred.
  • Experience assembling electronic racks, wiring cabinets, or building cable harnesses.
  • Ability to work independently, follow build instructions, and manage multiple assignments.

U.S. PERSON REQUIREMENTS

Due to compliance with U.S. export control laws and regulations, candidate must be a U.S. person, which is defined as, a U.S. citizen, a U.S. permanent resident, or have protected status in the U.S. under asylum or refugee status. ​

BENEFITS OF WORKING FOR HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Beyond a performance-driven salary, you'll work alongside dedicated experts on technology that's advancing aviation. As a Honeywell Aerospace employee, you're eligible for a comprehensive benefits package that includes:

  • Employer-subsidized medical, dental, vision and life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • 401(k) match, flexible spending accounts and health savings accounts
  • Employee assistance program and educational assistance
  • Parental leave and 12 paid holidays
  • Paid time off for vacation, personal and sick time

Explore your benefits:

ABOUT HONEYWELL AEROSPACE

Join a company that's reintroducing itself to the aviation community we've helped advance for more than a century. At Honeywell Aerospace (NASDAQ: HONA), we're launching as an independent, publicly traded aerospace and defense company built on a legacy of operational excellence and mission-focused execution.

Our new brand identity pairs that heritage with real momentum, as we build technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. With our systems on board 90% of the world's aircraft, your work here has reach that's rare to find anywhere else.

Focusing on our customers, investing in innovation, and building a culture of accountability and performance is how we're shaping what comes next.

Every horizon. Every mission. Every day.

ABOUT THE BUSINESS UNIT

Honeywell Aerospace products and services are found on aircraft across commercial aviation, defense and space — from engines and cockpit electronics to cabin systems, mechanical components and connectivity solutions. Our technology helps operators fly more safely, reduce fuel consumption, improve on-time performance and deliver a better experience for the people on board.

As aviation continues to evolve, we're also developing systems to support autonomous and supersonic platforms, bringing the same focus on safety and efficiency to the next era of flight. With approximately 36,000 employees worldwide and net sales of $17.4B in 2025, Honeywell Aerospace is one of the largest dedicated aerospace companies in the world. Explore our businesses: https://www.honeywellaerospace.com

Control Systems develops the thermal and motion control systems that help aircraft take off, land safely and protect the people on board. With more than 10 million passengers per day flying on aircraft equipped with our products and more than 75% of commercial flights beginning with our engine start systems, Control Systems reaches farther across the aviation industry than most people realize.

title: Industrial Engineering Intern (Summer 2027)
description:
About the role

Summer internships will range between the months of May and September depending on university schedules. Internship is full-time and on-site in San Jose, California.

The Assembly, Integration and Test (AIT) team at Muon is responsible for the assembly, integration, and validation of spacecraft hardware through unit acceptance testing as well as spacecraft-level integration and testing. As an Industrial Engineering Intern, you will support the development and improvement of the processes, tools, and systems that enable Muon to efficiently build and test spacecraft at scale.

You will work closely with AIT, Manufacturing Engineering, Quality, Supply Chain, and Test Engineering teams to analyze production data, improve workflows, identify bottlenecks, develop capacity models, and implement process improvements. This is a hands-on opportunity to apply industrial engineering principles in a fast-growing spacecraft manufacturing environment and directly contribute to increasing production efficiency and throughput.

Muon is a small and fast growing startup which offers interns the experience to get direct mentorship and have real impact on our programs. As an intern, you'll collaborate with a dynamic team in a startup environment and have the chance to learn from some of the most accomplished and experienced aerospace professionals in the industry. We're committed to offering an experience where your decisions and contributions play a pivotal role in driving Muon's success.

Responsibilities

  • Analyze spacecraft assembly, integration, and test processes to identify opportunities to improve efficiency, quality, throughput, and scalability.

  • Collect and analyze production data to identify trends, bottlenecks, constraints, and opportunities for improvement.
  • Support development of production capacity and resource planning models for spacecraft assembly and test operations.
  • Assist with production scheduling, workflow optimization, and resource allocation across AIT operations.
  • Conduct time studies and process observations to establish baseline cycle times, labor requirements, and process performance.

  • Identify opportunities to improve material flow, kitting, tooling, workstation layout, and overall factory/lab utilization.
  • Develop dashboards, reports, and other data-driven tools to provide visibility into production performance and operational metrics.
  • Support root-cause investigations and corrective actions for production constraints, process inefficiencies, and recurring issues.
  • Partner with technicians and engineers to identify practical improvements to spacecraft assembly and test processes.
  • Support implementation and validation of process improvements on the production floor.
  • Assist with developing scalable processes and systems to support increasing spacecraft production volume.
  • Document process improvements and communicate findings and recommendations to cross-functional stakeholders.

Qualifications

  • Currently pursuing a Bachelor's or Master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, Operations Research, or a related technical field.
  • Strong understanding of engineering, manufacturing, and/or operations fundamentals.
  • Demonstrated analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to use data to identify process improvements.
  • Experience with Excel or similar tools for data analysis, modeling, and visualization.
  • Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with an ability to work effectively in a fast-paced, collaborative team environment.
  • Ability to work hands-on in a production, laboratory, or engineering environment.
  • Strong organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Ability to approach complex operational challenges from a first-principles perspective.

Nice-to-have Skills

  • Previous internship, co-op, research, or project experience in industrial engineering, manufacturing, operations, or production environments.
  • Experience with Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, Kaizen, value-stream mapping, or other continuous improvement methodologies.
  • Experience conducting time studies, capacity analysis, line balancing, or process optimization.
  • Experience with production planning, scheduling, or resource capacity modeling.
  • Experience with data visualization or analytics tools such as Python, SQL, Power BI, Tableau, or similar.
  • Experience with CAD or facility/workstation layout tools.
  • Experience developing automated spreadsheets, dashboards, or other operational tools.
  • Previous experience on technical project teams such as a CubeSat, rocketry, Formula SAE, Solar Car, or other hardware-focused engineering project.
  • Familiarity with manufacturing, assembly, integration, or test processes for complex electromechanical hardware.
  • Experience working in a cleanroom, laboratory, or aerospace manufacturing environment.

Pay range

Bachelor's students $40/hour

Master's $45/hour

PhD $50/hour

About Muon Space

Founded in 2021, Muon Space is an end-to-end Space Systems Provider that designs, builds, and operates LEO satellite constellations delivering mission-critical data. Our revolutionary, integrated technology stack enables customers to optimize every dimension of their missions for faster time-to-orbit and superior constellation remote sensing performance. Our state-of-the-art facility in the heart of Silicon Valley is optimized for manufacturing spacecraft and rapid, flexible payload integration at scale. From climate monitoring to national security, Muon Space is dedicated to delivering Earth Intelligence for a safer and more resilient world.

title: RF Components Engineer II
description:
About Varda

Low Earth orbit is open for business. Varda is accelerating the development of commercial space infrastructure, from in-orbit pharmaceutical processing to reliable and economical reentry capsules. Varda’s W-Series vehicles are built, designed, and operated by Varda in-house, including the pharmaceutical processing payloads, the capsules, the C-PICA heat shields, and the satellite buses.

From life-saving pharmaceuticals to more powerful fiber optics, there is a world of products used on Earth today that can only be manufactured in space. Varda is accelerating innovation in the orbital economy by creating both the products and infrastructure needed so space can directly benefit life on Earth. Our mission is to expand the economic bounds of humankind.

Our team is uniquely suited to accomplishing this goal, with leadership and staff comprised of veterans from SpaceX, Blue Origin, major pharmaceutical companies and Silicon Valley. Varda was founded in January 2021 by Will Bruey and Delian Asparouhov with significant backing from world class investors including Khosla Ventures, Lux Capital, Founders Fund, Caffeinated Capital, General Catalyst, and Also Capital.

Varda is headquartered in El Segundo, California, where we have offices and a production facility where our vehicles, equipment, and materials are built, integrated, and tested. Varda also has offices in Washington, DC and Huntsville, AL.

Join Varda, and work to create a bustling in-space ecosystem.

About This Role

As an RF Component Engineer at Varda, you will play a pivotal role in ensuring seamless connectivity between our satellite vehicles and ground stations. You will be responsible for the complete lifecycle of each RF component, collaborating closely with RF Systems Engineers to define component specifications and to either select or design the necessary hardware. Your work will be crucial in rigorously validating components before their deployment to space. This role requires a strong sense of ownership over your hardware, continually setting new standards for testing RF components before flight.

Some people say that you only have one chance to fly to space so you must be certain it will work. At Varda, we believe that the trip to space and back is the easiest trip our hardware takes. We stress our components above and beyond the levels it should expect to see in flight and we investigate our failures thoroughly. Come join our team and build quality electronics that you will get to see fly over and over again.

Responsibilities

  • Serve as the Responsible Engineer for RF flight components, including radios, power amplifiers, antennas and filters.
  • Collaborate with RF Systems Engineers to refine product specifications, select or design appropriate components, and oversee the entire product lifecycle.
  • Work closely with Flight Software, Structures, and Integration & Test teams to document cross-functional interface requirements for a successful deployment of hardware onto the flight vehicle.
  • Take ultimate ownership of product acceptance and qualification testing for space environments, including Thermal, Vibration, Shock, TVAC, and EMI.
  • Develop test software to automate equipment, stimulate, and measure component performance, ensuring consistent flight hardware readiness.
  • Conduct root cause analysis on test failures and implement comprehensive mitigation strategies for flight risks.

Basic Qualifications

  • B.S. in Electrical Engineering, RF Engineering, or a related field.
    • Open to candidates of all experience levels, with role and responsibility adjustments made accordingly.
  • Strong hands-on experience with RF test equipment including VNAs, spectrum analyzers, oscilloscopes, function generators, power meters and power supplies.
  • Familiarity with RF components including LNAs, power amplifiers, mixers, filters, oscillators/synthesizers, attenuators, and switches.
  • Experience designing and integrating RF components into complete transmit or receive signal chains.
  • Proven track record of extreme ownership over projects, leading them to successful completion.
  • Proficiency with Python, familiarity with test software libraries like PyVISA for communication with test equipment.
  • Demonstrated curiosity and commitment to exploring foundational concepts and pursuing detailed insights with diligence.

Preferred Skills and Experience

  • Prior experience standing up HITL testbeds, managing configuration control, and driving and operating system-level tests.
  • Familiarity with Unix environments.
  • Experience developing test cases and test equipment to meet vehicle operating conditions.
  • Experience operating environmental test equipment (vibration shakers, TVAC chambers, or thermal chambers).
  • Strong project or program management skills.
  • Thrive in a dynamic work environment that values teamwork, innovation, and tackling challenges head-on. Be prepared for exposure to diverse tasks and a commitment to personal and professional growth.

Pay Range

  • Salary range:
    • Engineer II: $144,020 - $184,026/per year
  • This role is on-site in El Segundo, CA
  • Leveling and base salary is determined by job-related skills, education level, experience level, and job performance
  • You will be eligible for long-term incentives in the form of stock options and/or long-term cash awards

Consider your benefits covered for launch. At Varda, we invest in benefits and perks that support your health, financial well-being, and life beyond work. Benefits vary by position, with packages designed specifically for our regular full-time employees and interns.

Leading a team responsible for alumni programming, lifelong learning, and event strategy and execution, the Executive Director establishes a shared vision, develops talent, and fosters a collaborative, high-performing culture that advances Wharton's engagement goals. Responsible for the short- and long-term development and implementation of Wharton's alumni learning and programming strategy, the Executive Director ensures content is relevant, accessible, and aligned with institutional priorities. Working closely with faculty and school leadership, the Executive Director translates Wharton's research, thought leadership, and strategic priorities into compelling programming that resonates with alumni and donors and advances lifelong engagement.

Setting the vision for alumni-facing content across regional events, reunions, and global programs, the Executive Director identifies opportunities to connect faculty expertise, institutional priorities, and alumni interests to create meaningful, high-impact engagement experiences. In partnership with stakeholders across Alumni Relations, Development, Principal Gifts & Board Relations, Executive Education, academic departments, the Dean's Office, and faculty leadership, the Executive Director develops, shapes, and delivers programming that reflects Wharton's academic excellence while supporting the school's engagement and fundraising priorities.

As a member of the External Affairs leadership team reporting to the Chief Advancement Officer, the Executive Director collaborates with senior leaders across External Affairs and works closely with the Executive Director of Institutional and Strategic Events to ensure alignment across alumni, donor, and institutional engagement. The Executive Director also oversees the integration of content and events strategy, manages resources and budgets, and leads the team responsible for execution, ensuring programs advance engagement and fundraising goals while connecting Wharton's research, thought leadership, and strategic priorities with meaningful alumni and donor experiences.

As the senior leader accountable for the overall strategy, performance, and results of External Affairs’ alumni programming, lifelong learning, and events portfolio, the Executive Director advises the Chief Advancement Officer and External Affairs leadership on alumni engagement, lifelong learning, and event strategy. The role brings constituent insights, program performance, emerging trends, and leading practices to inform broader advancement strategy and priorities, and translates those insights into recommendations and new approaches developed in partnership with the External Affairs senior leadership team. The portfolio serves Wharton’s global alumni community through an integrated engagement strategy spanning in-person and virtual channels.

**Required Qualifications**

- Bachelor's degree and over 10 years of experience, or equivalent combination of education and experience, is required.
- Leadership experience in alumni relations, advancement, executive education, higher education administration, events, content strategy, communications, or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience developing and executing strategic engagement initiatives, large-scale events, or educational programming for sophisticated audiences.
- Proven ability to collaborate effectively with senior leaders, faculty, volunteers, and cross-functional stakeholders to achieve shared objectives.
- Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to influence without direct authority across complex organizations.
- Experience developing content strategies and translating complex ideas into compelling educational or engagement experiences.
- Demonstrated leadership experience managing teams, budgets, and multiple concurrent initiatives while balancing competing priorities.
- Strong analytical and strategic planning skills, including the ability to use data and audience insights to inform programming decisions.
- Understanding of advancement, alumni relations, and fundraising strategies, including the role of engagement programming in strengthening constituent relationships and philanthropic outcomes.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Experience working in higher education, academic medicine, or another complex, mission-driven organization.
- Experience partnering directly with faculty, researchers, or academic leadership to develop educational programming or thought leadership initiatives.
- Demonstrated understanding of how alumni engagement, donor stewardship, lifelong learning, and fundraising strategies intersect.
- Experience creating executive-level content and experiences that align institutional priorities with audience interests.
- Familiarity with advancement, alumni relations, or constituent engagement within a research university.
- Experience overseeing global or geographically distributed engagement programs.

**Job Location - City, State**

Philadelphia, Pennsylvania

**Department / School**

Wharton School

$135,327.00 - $170,000.00 Annual Rate

Salary offers are made based on the candidate’s qualifications, experience, skills, and education as they directly relate to the requirements of the position, and in alignment with salary ranges based on external market data for the job’s level. You can also use flexible spending accounts to pay for eligible health care and dependent care expenses with pre-tax dollars.

If you apply when you’re newly hired, you won’t have to provide proof of good health or be subject to underwriting requirements. title: Customer Care medewerker
description:
Onze klant gelegen te Antwerpen is actief in verzekeringen.


Jobomschrijving

Customer Care Medewerker | Antwerpen

Wil jij elke dag écht het verschil maken voor mensen? Ben je klantgericht, administratief sterk én spreek je vloeiend Nederlands en Frans? Dan is deze functie als Customer Care Officer in Antwerpen misschien wel jouw volgende stap.

Jouw uitdaging

Als Customer Care Officer ben jij het eerste aanspreekpunt voor klanten en tussenpersonen. Dankzij jouw klantgerichte aanpak zorg je ervoor dat elke vraag correct en efficiënt wordt behandeld.

Jouw takenpakket bestaat onder andere uit:

  • Je beantwoordt inkomende telefoongesprekken of verbindt klanten door naar de juiste collega.
  • Je behandelt e-mails en andere schriftelijke vragen op een professionele manier.
  • Je voert diverse administratieve taken uit en zoekt de nodige informatie op om klanten correct verder te helpen.
  • Je helpt mee bij de dagelijkse werkverdeling binnen het team en zorgt samen met je collega's voor een vlotte permanentie.
  • Je luistert naar de behoeften van klanten en denkt actief mee aan de beste oplossing.
  • Je draagt bij aan een kwalitatieve en warme dienstverlening waarin de klant altijd centraal staat.

Wie ben jij?

Jij haalt energie uit het helpen van mensen en werkt graag nauwkeurig. Daarnaast herken je jezelf in het volgende:

  • Je beschikt over een bachelordiploma of hebt minstens twee jaar relevante ervaring in een klantgerichte administratieve functie.
  • Je werkt vlot met verschillende computerprogramma's.
  • Je communiceert vloeiend in het Nederlands én Frans.
  • Je bent vriendelijk, commercieel ingesteld en denkt steeds in oplossingen.
  • Je werkt nauwkeurig, gestructureerd en administratief correct.
  • Je bent een echte teamspeler, maar kan ook zelfstandig verantwoordelijkheid opnemen.
  • Je bent flexibel en past je gemakkelijk aan in een dynamische werkomgeving.

title: Program Controls Analyst III
description:
As a Program Controls Specialist III here at Honeywell Aerospace, you will play a critical role in leading the control and oversight of complex project elements including scheduling, cost management, and adherence to earned value management principles to ensure program success. You will be an integral part of a dynamic team that exemplifies Honeywell Aerospace’s commitment to innovation, operational excellence, and shaping the future of aviation technology.

Honeywell Aerospace is focused on delivering cutting-edge technology that helps pilots navigate with confidence, aircraft operate more efficiently, and operators stay ahead of change. Your advanced expertise in program controls will directly support these goals, driving projects that significantly impact the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of the aerospace industry worldwide.

You will report directly to our Program Controls Manager and you’ll work out of our Deer Valley, AZ location on a Hybrid work schedule.

In this role, you will influence program efficiency and accuracy by providing expert program controls leadership, enabling effective decision-making, and contributing to the timely and cost-effective delivery of aerospace projects.

Key Responsibilities

  • Leads or supports the development of initial program baselines, program re-baselines and compliant baseline change management
  • Prepares and analyzes reliable cost report data for program stakeholders
  • Responsible for program EAC (estimate at completion) management
  • Ensures cost and schedule integration are aligned to scope and contract requirements
  • Proactively and effectively communicates with program team and customers
  • Responsible for reliable program EVM (earned value management) application, compliance and procedures
  • Actively supports program issue identification, root cause, impact analysis and recommends corrective actions
  • Actively supports CAMs in monthly cost and schedule reviews and drives complete and accurate EACs and variance analysis
  • Initiates and participates in organizational and program improvements
  • Mentors other team members

YOU MUST HAVE

  • 4 year's experience EVM (Earned Value Management)
  • Required to attain PMP certification within 6 months of start date.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook).

WE VALUE

  • Experience in usage of Earned Value (EV) metrics, managing budgets and milestone fidelity
  • Ability to influence program stakeholders at varying levels across the organization
  • Ability to convey subtle or complex messages clearly, as appropriate for the topic and audience
  • User experience of SAP system
  • Experience in financial data compilation, analysis and metrics management

  • Cost Reporting Generation: CPR, IPMR, IPMDAR, CFSR

title: Purchasing Coordinator
description:
About Us

HelloConnect

HelloConnect is a subsidiary of HelloFresh, founded to address years of challenges faced in its own customer care. Leveraging our extensive experience in developing customer care tailored to the immediate needs of HelloFresh, our solutions are hyper-focused on serving high-growth companies. Located in Manila, Philippines, we are now making this service available to other companies to benefit from our experience, scale, cost savings, and service level improvements.

HelloFresh

HelloFresh is a global leader in delivering delicious meal kits and grocery boxes straight to customers' doorsteps. We are dedicated to providing high-quality, convenient, and sustainable meal solutions that inspire people to cook and eat healthy at home. Our commitment to innovation and customer satisfaction drives our ongoing success.

POSITION SUMMARY

Have you ever wondered how HelloFresh delivers thousands of meal boxes to customers' doorsteps? Are you passionate about Supply Chain and Planning, and hope to impact the experience of thousands of customers? Are you obsessed with helping solving challenging problems and creating new solutions? If so, we look forward to hearing from you!

HelloFresh is looking for a Purchasing Coordinator to support our Supply Chain Operations in the generation of purchase orders for various HelloFresh markets across Europe, the UK, Australia and New Zealand. This role will ensure the accuracy and timeliness of our ordering processes using a combination of in-house tools and google suite packages. Working closely with the Supply Chain, Procurement and Forecasting teams, this role will raise, edit and send purchase orders to our suppliers.

Above all, we are looking for people who will make HelloFresh better. We believe there are many different ways of developing skills, and we love diverse experiences! So even if you don't tick all the boxes but think you'd thrive in this role, we would really like to learn more about you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Support our inbound supply chain operations & external partnerships to ensure our ingredients arrive at our customers on time and in full
  • Calculate and issue purchase orders for your category area(s). Revise or raise additional purchase orders as required
  • Complete the necessary audit checks to ensure orders are complete and accurate before sending to suppliers
  • Resolve any queries raised by suppliers on the purchase orders or transportation, and escalate where necessary
  • Resolve operational issues and perform root cause analysis. Put into place corrective actions to help prevent similar issues from recurring
  • Help to establish, create and maintain reports that support daily operations
  • Distribute forecast information to HelloFresh suppliers
  • Partner closely with the Suppliers and internal teams such as Forecasting, Procurement, Warehouse and Inventory to ensure purchase orders are timely and fulfil customer requirements
  • Correct or escalate any data inaccuracies to your Line Manager
  • Report any tooling issues and recommend improvements
  • Maintain the confidentiality of our data and uphold the integrity of our business\
  • Support on additional day-to-day tasks as needed, including but not limited to, data entry, emergency
  • purchase orders, updates to delivery schedules and inventory data analysis
  • Remain flexible to changing duties and responsibilities as business needs vary

WHAT YOU'LL BRING

  • At least 2 years of previous purchasing experience as a Buyer
  • Requires expertise in operating Microsoft Office programs, and ideally ERP/MRP systems

SOFT SKILLS

  • Excellent verbal and written communication, collaboration, and self-management skills with a strong focus on teamwork.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and critical thinking skills
  • Assertive, responsible, and adaptable, with the ability to work in a fast-paced environment and navigate complex situations.
  • Great attention to detail and organisational skills
  • Hands on mentality
  • Initiative and proactivity

title: Sr Bioinformatics Scientist
description:
Senior Bioinformatics Scientist

Position Overview

Twist Bioscience is seeking a Senior Bioinformatics Scientist to join our Scientific Computing team supporting R&D across DNA Synthesis and Protein Solutions. You will develop computational methods and predictive models to understand biological and experimental data, guide product development, and improve scientific workflows.

Working at the intersection of computational and experimental biology, you will partner with scientists to investigate challenging questions across sequencing, DNA synthesis, and protein characterization. Your work will include developing algorithms, testing hypotheses, evaluating new methods, and building reproducible analysis workflows.

We are looking for a curious scientist with strong computational skills and sound scientific judgment who enjoys learning new biology and turning open-ended questions into actionable insights.

Key Responsibilities

  • Develop novel computational methods and algorithms supporting DNA synthesis, sequence analysis, and protein characterization.
  • Partner with experimental scientists to formulate hypotheses, design experiments, and interpret results that guide product and process development.
  • Analyze NGS and other experimental datasets to identify biological patterns, understand sources of variability, and investigate unexpected outcomes.
  • Apply statistical methods, machine learning, and predictive modeling to connect sequence and experimental features with product quality and performance.
  • Evaluate and validate analytical approaches, including their accuracy, limitations, and applicability across experimental conditions.
  • Develop reproducible analysis pipelines using Nextflow and other scientific computing tools to support research and method evaluation.
  • Communicate findings and recommendations to scientific and cross-functional stakeholders, and collaborate with engineers to translate successful methods into broader use.
  • Explore new technologies and analytical approaches as research priorities evolve.

Required Qualifications

  • Ph.D. with 3+ years, Master’s degree with 6+ years, or Bachelor’s degree with 8+ years of relevant experience in bioinformatics, computational biology, biostatistics, or a related field; equivalent combinations of education and experience will be considered.
  • Strong Python programming skills and experience analyzing biological or experimental data.
  • Hands-on experience with NGS analysis and a solid understanding of molecular biology.
  • Experience developing and evaluating computational algorithms, statistical methods, or predictive models.
  • Strong foundation in statistics, experimental design, and critical interpretation of scientific results.
  • Experience building reproducible analysis workflows using Nextflow or a comparable tool.
  • Demonstrated ability to independently investigate scientific problems and learn unfamiliar methods or biological domains.
  • Ability to collaborate closely with experimental scientists and communicate complex findings clearly.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience with protein data analysis, DNA synthesis, or sequence design.
  • Experience applying machine learning to biological data, including rigorous validation.
  • Experience working with high-throughput experimental datasets and integrating multiple data types.
  • Familiarity with cloud computing and scalable scientific workflows.
  • A track record of developing computational methods that inform experimental decisions or improve products.

We welcome candidates with depth in a relevant scientific area and the curiosity and quantitative foundation to contribute across disciplines.

About Twist Bioscience

Twist Bioscience synthesizes genes from scratch, known as “writing” DNA. Just as children learn to both read and write, the next phase of development for the genomics revolution is the ability to write DNA.

At Twist Bioscience, we work in service of people who are changing the world for the better. In fields such as health care, agriculture, industrial chemicals and data storage, our unique silicon-based DNA Synthesis Platform provides precision at a scale that is otherwise unavailable to our customers.

In this role, you will collaborate with a team to execute project plans related to optical systems and test systems, ensuring all engineering requirements are fulfilled. You will provide technical assistance to fellow engineers, troubleshoot issues, and lead or contribute to the development of innovative solutions for complex customer challenges. This position requires a blend of hands-on, in-person laboratory work and activities outside the lab, including conceptual discussions and model-based analysis, to support team members and complete your own independent tasks.

  • Conduct system requirements analysis and define the specifications necessary for the development of optical payload systems.
  • Oversee the development of test plans and procedures and ensure thorough testing of optical components and systems.
